translations.idiomatic: Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance, Volume 87

sentences.zh: 【晉紀九】起屠維大荒落，盡重光協洽，凡三年。

translations.literal: [Jin Records 9] From Tuyi Dahuangluo through Chongguang Xieqia, three years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Records of Jin, Number Nine] Spanning from the cyclical year Tuyi Dahuangluo through Chongguang Xieqia—three years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝中永嘉三年（

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part, Yongjia Year Three (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part—Yongjia, Year Three (

sentences.zh: 己巳，公元三零九年）

translations.literal: jisi, CE 309)
translations.idiomatic: jisi, 309 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，辛丑朔，熒惑犯紫微。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day xinchou, Mars encroached upon the Purple Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the new moon of xinchou, Mars encroached upon the Purple Palace constellation.

sentences.zh: 漢太史令宣於修之，言於漢主淵曰：「不出三年，必克洛陽。

translations.literal: The Han Grand Astrologer Xuanyu Xiuzhi said to the Han ruler Liu Yuan: "Within three years Luoyang will surely be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyu Xiuzhi, Grand Astrologer of Han, said to Liu Yuan, ruler of Han: "Within three years Luoyang will surely fall.

sentences.zh: 蒲子崎嶇，難以久安；

translations.literal: Puzi is rugged and steep, difficult to dwell in for long;
translations.idiomatic: Puzi is rugged and forbidding, unsuited to a lasting capital;

sentences.zh: 平陽氣象方昌，請徙都之。」

translations.literal: Pingyang's vital energy is now flourishing; I request that the capital be moved there."
translations.idiomatic: Pingyang's fortunes are on the rise—I urge that the capital be moved there."

sentences.zh: 淵從之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan followed his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元河瑞。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Herui.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared, and the era name was changed to Herui.

sentences.zh: 三月，戊申，高密孝王略薨。

translations.literal: In the third month, on wushen, Prince Xiao of Gaomi, Sima Lue, died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on wushen, Sima Lue, Prince Xiao of Gaomi, died.

sentences.zh: 以尚書左僕射山簡為征南將軍、都督荊、湘、交、廣四州諸軍事，鎮襄陽。

translations.literal: Shan Jian, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was appointed General Who Conquers the South, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in the four provinces of Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang, and stationed at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian, Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing, was made General Who Conquers the South, given overall command of military affairs in Jing, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang, and posted at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 簡，濤之子也，嗜酒，不恤政事；

translations.literal: Shan Jian was the son of Shan Tao; he was fond of wine and paid no heed to government affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Shan Jian was Shan Tao's son—a man who loved his wine and cared nothing for the business of government;

sentences.zh: 表「順陽內史劉璠得眾心，恐百姓劫璠為主」。

translations.literal: he memorialized that "Liu Fan, Administrator of Shunyang, has won the hearts of the people, and I fear the common folk may seize him and make him their leader."
translations.idiomatic: he submitted a memorial warning that "Liu Fan, Administrator of Shunyang, has won the people's loyalty, and I fear the populace may force him to become their leader."

sentences.zh: 詔征璠為越騎校尉。

translations.literal: An edict summoned Liu Fan to serve as Commandant of the Swift Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled Liu Fan to the capital as Commandant of the Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 南州由是遂亂，父老莫不追思劉弘。

translations.literal: The southern provinces thereupon fell into disorder, and none among the elders failed to look back with longing upon Liu Hong.
translations.idiomatic: The southern provinces thereupon fell into chaos, and everywhere the elders looked back with longing upon Liu Hong.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，太傅越自滎陽入京師。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Grand Tutor Sima Yue entered the capital from Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Grand Tutor Sima Yue entered the capital from Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 中書監王敦謂所親曰：「太傅專執威權，而選用表請，尚書猶以舊制裁之，今日之來，必有所誅。」

translations.literal: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Wang Dun said to those close to him: "The Grand Tutor monopolizes authority, yet when he submits nominations and requests, the Masters of Writing still restrain him by the old regulations. His coming today will surely bring executions."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dun, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing, told his intimates: "The Grand Tutor holds all real power, yet when he submits nominations and requests, the Masters of Writing still check him under the old rules. His arrival today will surely mean bloodshed."

sentences.zh: 帝之為太弟也，與中庶子繆播親善，及即位，以播為中書監，繆胤為太僕卿，委以心膂；

translations.literal: When the emperor had been Heir Exalted, he had been on close terms with Attendant of the Heir Exalted Mi Bo; upon ascending the throne, he appointed Mi Bo Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Mi Yin Minister of the Household for the Imperial Stud, entrusting them as his innermost confidants;
translations.idiomatic: While still Heir Exalted, the emperor had been close to Mi Bo, Attendant of the Heir Exalted; once enthroned, he made Mi Bo Supervisor of the Masters of Writing and Mi Yin Minister of the Household for the Imperial Stud, trusting them as his innermost advisers;

sentences.zh: 帝舅散騎常侍王延、尚書何綏、太史令高堂沖，並參機密。

translations.literal: the emperor's maternal uncle Wang Yan, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry, He Sui of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Astrologer Gaotang Chong all shared in confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor's uncle by marriage Wang Yan, Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry, He Sui of the Masters of Writing, and Grand Astrologer Gaotang Chong were all privy to state secrets.

sentences.zh: 越疑朝臣貳於己，劉輿、潘滔勸越悉誅播等。

translations.literal: Sima Yue suspected the court officials of disloyalty to him; Liu Yu and Pan Tao urged him to execute Mi Bo and the others entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue suspected the court officials of being disloyal to him; Liu Yu and Pan Tao urged him to put Mi Bo and his circle to death.

sentences.zh: 越乃誣播等欲為亂，乙丑，遣平東將軍王秉，帥甲士三千入宮，執播等十餘人於帝側，付廷尉，殺之。

translations.literal: Sima Yue then falsely accused Mi Bo and the others of plotting rebellion; on yichou he dispatched General Who Pacifies the East Wang Bing, leading three thousand armored troops into the palace, seized more than ten men including Mi Bo at the emperor's side, handed them to the Minister of Justice, and had them killed.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue then framed Mi Bo and the others for plotting rebellion; on yichou he sent General Who Pacifies the East Wang Bing at the head of three thousand armored troops into the palace, seized more than a dozen men including Mi Bo at the emperor's side, turned them over to the Minister of Justice, and had them executed.

sentences.zh: 帝歎息流涕而已。

translations.literal: The emperor could only sigh and weep.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could only sigh and weep.

sentences.zh: 綏，曾之孫也。

translations.literal: He Sui was the grandson of He Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: He Sui was the grandson of He Zeng.

sentences.zh: 初，何曾侍武帝宴，退，謂諸子曰：「主上開創大業，吾每宴見，未嘗聞經國遠圖，惟說平生常事，非貽厥孫謀之道也，及身而已，後嗣其殆乎！

translations.literal: Earlier, when He Zeng attended Emperor Wu at a banquet and withdrew, he told his sons: "Our lord has founded a great enterprise, yet whenever I attend him at banquet I never hear talk of far-reaching plans for governing the state—only accounts of everyday affairs from his own life. This is not the way to bequeath counsel to one's descendants; it extends no further than his own person. His heirs are likely in peril!
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after attending Emperor Wu at a banquet, He Zeng told his sons on returning home: "Our lord has founded a great enterprise, yet whenever I dine with him I never hear a far-reaching plan for governing the realm—only stories from his own life. That is no way to leave counsel for one's descendants; it reaches no further than his own person. His heirs are likely doomed!

sentences.zh: 汝輩猶可以免。」

translations.literal: You may still escape harm."
translations.idiomatic: You may yet escape harm."

sentences.zh: 指諸孫曰：「此屬必及於難。」

translations.literal: Pointing to his grandsons he said: "These will surely meet with disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Pointing to his grandsons, he said: "These will surely come to grief."

sentences.zh: 及綏死，兄嵩哭之曰：「我祖其殆聖乎！」

translations.literal: When He Sui died, his elder brother He Song wept over him and said: "Was our grandfather nearly a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: When He Sui died, his elder brother He Song mourned him, saying: "Our grandfather was nearly a sage!"

sentences.zh: 曾日食萬錢，猶雲無下箸處。

translations.literal: He Zeng's daily food cost ten thousand cash, yet he still complained there was nothing worth picking up his chopsticks for.
translations.idiomatic: He Zeng spent ten thousand cash a day on food, yet still complained that nothing on the table was worth picking up his chopsticks for.

sentences.zh: 子劭，日食二萬。

translations.literal: His son He Shao spent twenty thousand a day.
translations.idiomatic: His son He Shao spent twenty thousand a day.

sentences.zh: 綏及弟機、羨，汰侈尤甚；

translations.literal: He Sui and his brothers Ji and Xian were even more extravagant in their excess;
translations.idiomatic: He Sui and his brothers Ji and Xian were even more ruinously extravagant;

sentences.zh: 與人書疏，詞禮簡傲。

translations.literal: in letters to others their language and courtesy were terse and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: in their letters to others their tone was curt and haughty.

sentences.zh: 河內王尼見綏書，謂人曰：「伯蔚居亂世而矜豪乃爾，其能免乎？」

translations.literal: Wang Ni of Henei, seeing He Sui's letter, said to someone: "Boyu in such troubled times flaunts his pride like this—can he escape ruin?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni of Henei, reading He Sui's letter, said to someone: "Boyu flaunts his arrogance in such troubled times—can he possibly escape disaster?"

sentences.zh: 人曰：「伯蔚聞卿言，必相危害。」

translations.literal: The man said: "If Boyu hears what you say, he will surely do you harm."
translations.idiomatic: The man replied: "If Boyu hears you, he will surely retaliate against you."

sentences.zh: 尼曰：「伯蔚比聞我言，自己死矣！」

translations.literal: Wang Ni said: "By the time Boyu hears my words, he will already be dead!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ni said: "By the time Boyu hears my words, he will already be dead!"

sentences.zh: 及永嘉之末，何氏無遺種。

translations.literal: By the end of the Yongjia era, not a single member of the He clan survived.
translations.idiomatic: By the end of the Yongjia era, not one member of the He clan remained.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：何曾譏武帝偷惰，取過目前，不為遠慮；

translations.literal: Your subject Guang remarks: He Zeng mocked Emperor Wu for indolence, content to get through the present moment without far-sighted planning;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang comments: He Zeng mocked Emperor Wu for indolence—content to scrape through the present without looking ahead;

sentences.zh: 知天下將亂，子孫必與其憂，何其明也！

translations.literal: knowing the realm would fall into chaos and that his descendants would surely share in its woes—how perceptive he was!
translations.idiomatic: knowing the realm would fall into chaos and that his descendants would share in its suffering—how perceptive he was!

sentences.zh: 然身為僭侈，使子孫承流，卒以驕奢亡族，其明安在哉！

translations.literal: Yet he himself lived in extravagant excess, letting his descendants follow in the same current, until at last the clan perished through pride and luxury—where then was his wisdom!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he himself lived in extravagant excess and let his descendants drift in the same current, until at last the whole clan perished through pride and luxury—where then was his wisdom!

sentences.zh: 且身為宰相，知其君之過，不以告而私語於家，非忠臣也。

translations.literal: Moreover, serving as chief minister, knowing his ruler's faults yet not reporting them but speaking privately at home—this was no loyal subject.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, as chief minister he knew his ruler's faults yet never reported them, confining his criticism to private talk at home—this was no loyal subject.

sentences.zh: 太傅越以王敦為揚州刺史。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue appointed Wang Dun Inspector of Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue appointed Wang Dun Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 劉實連年請老，朝廷不許。

translations.literal: Liu Shi for successive years requested retirement on account of age, but the court would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year Liu Shi asked to retire on account of age, but the court refused.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞劉坦上言：「古之養老，以不事為憂，不以吏之為重，謂宜聽實所守。」

translations.literal: Liu Tan, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial: "In antiquity, honoring the aged meant relieving them of duties, not burdening them with office; I submit that Liu Shi should be allowed to retire to his fief."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan, Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing, submitted a memorial: "In antiquity, honoring the aged meant freeing them from burdens of office, not weighing them down with posts; Liu Shi should be allowed to retire to his fief."

sentences.zh: 丁卯，詔實以侯就第。

translations.literal: On dingmao, an edict ordered Liu Shi to retire to his estate as a marquis.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, an edict permitted Liu Shi to retire to his estate as a marquis.

sentences.zh: 以王衍為太尉。

translations.literal: Wang Yan was appointed Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan was appointed Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 太傅越解兗州牧，領司徒。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue relinquished the governorship of Yan Province and assumed the post of Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue gave up the governorship of Yan Province and took up the post of Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 越以頃來興事，多由殿省，乃奏宿衛有侯爵者皆罷之。

translations.literal: Sima Yue, because recent undertakings had often been thwarted by the palace guard offices, memorialized that all guardsmen holding marquisates should be dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Because recent undertakings had often been blocked by the palace guard offices, Sima Yue memorialized that all guardsmen holding marquisates should be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 時殿中武官並封侯，由是出者略盡，皆泣涕而去。

translations.literal: At the time all martial officers of the palace guard held enfeoffed ranks as marquises; as a result nearly all who departed did so in tears.
translations.idiomatic: At the time all martial officers of the palace guard held marquisates; nearly all who were dismissed left in tears.

sentences.zh: 更使右衛將軍何倫、左衛將軍王秉領東海國兵數百人宿衛。

translations.literal: He then had Right Guard General He Lun and Left Guard General Wang Bing lead several hundred troops of Donghai commandery as the new palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He then replaced them with Right Guard General He Lun and Left Guard General Wang Bing, who led several hundred troops from Donghai commandery as the new palace guard.

sentences.zh: 左積弩將軍朱誕奔漢，具陳洛陽孤弱，勸漢主淵攻之。

translations.literal: Left Crossbow General Zhu Dan defected to Han, fully describing Luoyang's isolation and weakness, and urged the Han ruler Liu Yuan to attack it.
translations.idiomatic: Left Crossbow General Zhu Dan defected to Han, describing in detail how isolated and weak Luoyang was, and urged Liu Yuan to attack it.

sentences.zh: 淵以誕為前鋒都督，以滅晉大將軍劉景為大都督，將兵攻黎陽，克之；

translations.literal: Liu Yuan made Zhu Dan Vanguard Commander-in-Chief and General Who Destroys Jin Liu Jing Grand Commander-in-Chief; they led troops to attack Liyang, took it;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan made Zhu Dan Vanguard Commander-in-Chief and General Who Destroys Jin Liu Jing Grand Commander-in-Chief; they led troops against Liyang and captured it;

sentences.zh: 又敗王堪於延津，沈男女三萬餘人於河。

translations.literal: and again defeated Wang Kan at Yanjin, drowning more than thirty thousand men and women in the river.
translations.idiomatic: and again defeated Wang Kan at Yanjin, drowning more than thirty thousand men and women in the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 淵聞之，怒曰：「景何面復見朕？

translations.literal: When Liu Yuan heard of this, he said in anger: "With what face can Jing come before me again?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuan heard of this, he said in fury: "How dare Jing show his face before me again?

sentences.zh: 且天道豈能容之？

translations.literal: Moreover, how could Heaven's way tolerate such a deed?
translations.idiomatic: And how could Heaven tolerate such a deed?

sentences.zh: 吾所欲除者，司馬氏耳，細民何罪？」

translations.literal: Those I wish to destroy are the Sima clan—what crime have the common people committed?"
translations.idiomatic: Those I mean to destroy are the Sima clan—what crime have the common people committed?"

sentences.zh: 黜景為平虜將軍。

translations.literal: Liu Jing was demoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jing was demoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians.

sentences.zh: 夏，大旱，江、漢、河、洛皆竭，可涉。

translations.literal: In summer a great drought occurred; the Yangtze, Han, Yellow, and Luo rivers all ran dry, so that one could wade across.
translations.idiomatic: In summer a great drought struck; the Yangtze, Han, Yellow, and Luo rivers all ran dry, so that one could wade across them.

sentences.zh: 漢安東大將軍石勒寇巨鹿、常山，眾至十餘萬，集衣冠人物，別為君子營。

translations.literal: Han General Who Pacifies the East Shi Le raided Julu and Changshan; his forces reached more than one hundred thousand; he gathered men of official rank and set them apart in a separate Gentlemen's Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, Han General Who Pacifies the East, raided Julu and Changshan; his forces swelled to more than one hundred thousand; he gathered men of official rank and set them apart in a separate Gentlemen's Camp.

sentences.zh: 以趙郡張賓為謀主，刁膺為股肱，夔安、孔萇、支雄、桃豹、逯明為爪牙，并州諸胡羯多從之。

translations.literal: He made Zhang Bin of Zhao commandery his chief strategist, Diao Ying his right-hand man, and Kuai An, Kong Chang, Zhi Xiong, Tao Bao, and Lu Ming his claws and teeth; many of the Hu and Jie peoples of Bing Province followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He made Zhang Bin of Zhao commandery his chief strategist, Diao Ying his right-hand man, and Kuai An, Kong Chang, Zhi Xiong, Tao Bao, and Lu Ming his lieutenants; many of the Hu and Jie peoples of Bing Province rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 初，張賓好讀書，闊達有大志，常自比張子房。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Bin loved reading; he was broad-minded and had great ambitions, and often compared himself to Zhang Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhang Bin was a devoted reader—broad-minded and ambitious—and often compared himself to Zhang Liang.

sentences.zh: 及石勒徇山東，賓謂所親曰：「吾歷觀諸將，無如此胡將軍者，可與共成大業！」

translations.literal: When Shi Le swept through the lands east of the mountains, Zhang Bin said to those close to him: "I have surveyed all the generals, and none is like this barbarian general—I can achieve a great enterprise with him!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le swept through the lands east of the mountains, Zhang Bin told his intimates: "I have looked over all the generals, and none compares with this barbarian commander—I can build a great enterprise with him!"

sentences.zh: 乃提劍詣軍門，大呼請見，勒亦未之奇也。

translations.literal: He then took up his sword and went to the army gate, shouting to request an audience; Shi Le at first thought nothing special of him.
translations.idiomatic: He then took up his sword, went to the army gate, and shouted to request an audience; at first Shi Le saw nothing remarkable in him.

sentences.zh: 賓數以策干勒，已而皆如所言。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin repeatedly presented strategies to Shi Le, and in time all proved as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin repeatedly offered strategies to Shi Le, and in time every one proved exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 勒由是奇之，署為軍功曹，動靜咨之。

translations.literal: Shi Le thereupon marveled at him, appointed him Army Merit Officer, and consulted him on every move.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le thereupon came to marvel at him, appointed him Army Merit Officer, and consulted him on every decision.

sentences.zh: 漢主淵以王彌為侍中、都督青、徐、兗、豫、荊、揚六州諸軍事、征東大將軍、青州牧，與楚王聰共攻壺關，以石勒為前鋒都督。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Yuan appointed Wang Mi Palace Attendant, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in the six provinces of Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang, General Who Conquers the East, and Governor of Qing Province; together with Prince of Chu Liu Cong he attacked Huguan Pass, with Shi Le as Vanguard Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan appointed Wang Mi Palace Attendant, gave him overall command of military affairs in Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang, made him General Who Conquers the East and Governor of Qing Province, and together with Prince of Chu Liu Cong attacked Huguan Pass, with Shi Le as Vanguard Commander-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 劉琨遣護軍黃肅、韓述救之，聰敗述於西澗，勒敗肅於封田，皆殺之。

translations.literal: Liu Kun dispatched Protector of the Army Huang Su and Han Shu to the rescue; Liu Cong defeated Han Shu at Xijian, and Shi Le defeated Huang Su at Fengtian; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun sent Protector of the Army Huang Su and Han Shu to the rescue; Liu Cong defeated Han Shu at Xijian, and Shi Le defeated Huang Su at Fengtian; both were killed.

sentences.zh: 太傅越遣淮南內史王曠、將軍施融、曹超將兵拒聰等。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue dispatched Wang Kuang, Administrator of Huainan, and the generals Shi Rong and Cao Chao with troops to resist Liu Cong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue sent Wang Kuang, Administrator of Huainan, and the generals Shi Rong and Cao Chao with troops to resist Liu Cong and his forces.

sentences.zh: 曠濟河，欲長驅而前，融曰：「彼乘險間出，我雖有數萬之眾，猶是一軍獨受敵也。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang crossed the river and wished to drive straight ahead; Shi Rong said: "They are exploiting the terrain to strike from an unexpected angle; though we have tens of thousands of men, we would still be a single army facing the enemy alone.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang crossed the river and wanted to press straight ahead; Shi Rong said: "They are using the terrain to strike from an unexpected angle; though we have tens of thousands of men, we would still be one army facing the enemy alone.

sentences.zh: 且當阻水為固以量形勢，然後圖之。」

translations.literal: We should first hold the river as a firm barrier to assess the situation, and only then plan our move."
translations.idiomatic: We should first hold the river as a firm line, assess the situation, and only then decide our next move."

sentences.zh: 曠怒曰：「君欲沮眾邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Kuang said angrily: "Do you mean to discourage the troops!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang snapped: "Are you trying to discourage the troops!"

sentences.zh: 融退，曰：「彼善用兵，曠暗於事勢，吾屬今必死矣！」

translations.literal: Shi Rong withdrew and said: "They know how to use troops; Wang Kuang is blind to the situation—we are surely doomed!"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Rong withdrew and said: "They know how to fight; Wang Kuang is blind to the situation—we are surely doomed!"

sentences.zh: 曠等逾太行與聰遇，戰於長平之間，曠兵大敗，融、超皆死。

translations.literal: Wang Kuang and the others crossed the Taihang range and encountered Liu Cong; they fought between Changping; Wang Kuang's army was utterly defeated, and Shi Rong and Cao Chao both died.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kuang and his men crossed the Taihang range and met Liu Cong; they fought in the region of Changping; Wang Kuang's army was routed, and Shi Rong and Cao Chao were both killed.

sentences.zh: 聰遂破屯留、長子，凡斬獲萬九千級。

translations.literal: Liu Cong thereupon captured Tunliu and Changzi; in all nineteen thousand heads and captives were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong thereupon captured Tunliu and Changzi; in all nineteen thousand heads and captives were taken.

sentences.zh: 上黨太守龐淳以壺關降漢。

translations.literal: Pang Chun, Administrator of Shangdang, surrendered Huguan Pass to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Chun, Administrator of Shangdang, surrendered Huguan Pass to Han.

sentences.zh: 劉琨以都尉張倚領上黨太守，據襄垣。

translations.literal: Liu Kun had Commandant Zhang Yi act as Administrator of Shangdang and hold Xiangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun had Commandant Zhang Yi serve as Administrator of Shangdang and hold Xiangyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，匈奴劉猛死，右賢王去卑子之誥升爰代領其眾。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Xiongnu Liu Meng died, Gaoshengyuan, son of the Right Worthy King Qubie, succeeded to command of his forces.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the Xiongnu leader Liu Meng died, Gaoshengyuan, son of the Right Worthy King Qubie, took command of his forces.

sentences.zh: 誥升爰卒，子虎立，居新興，號鐵弗氏，與白部鮮卑皆附於漢。

translations.literal: When Gaoshengyuan died, his son Hu established himself at Xinxing, taking the clan name Tiefu; he and the White Division Xianbei all submitted to Han.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaoshengyuan died, his son Hu established himself at Xinxing under the clan name Tiefu; he and the White Division Xianbei all submitted to Han.

sentences.zh: 劉琨自將擊虎，劉聰遣兵襲晉陽，不克。

translations.literal: Liu Kun personally led troops to attack Hu; Liu Cong dispatched troops to raid Jinyang but failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun personally led troops against Hu; Liu Cong sent troops to raid Jinyang but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 五月，漢主淵封子裕為齊王，隆為魯王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the Han ruler Liu Yuan enfeoffed his son Liu Yu as Prince of Qi and Liu Long as Prince of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Liu Yuan enfeoffed his son Liu Yu as Prince of Qi and Liu Long as Prince of Lu.

sentences.zh: 秋，八月，漢主淵命楚王聰等進攻洛陽；

translations.literal: In autumn, in the eighth month, the Han ruler Liu Yuan ordered Prince of Chu Liu Cong and the others to advance and attack Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the eighth month, Liu Yuan ordered Prince of Chu Liu Cong and the others to advance against Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 詔平北將軍曹武等拒之，皆為聰所敗。

translations.literal: an edict ordered General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu and the others to resist them; all were defeated by Liu Cong.
translations.idiomatic: an edict ordered General Who Pacifies the North Cao Wu and the others to resist them; Liu Cong defeated them all.

sentences.zh: 聰長驅至宜陽，自恃驟勝，怠不設備。

translations.literal: Liu Cong drove straight to Yiyang; trusting in his swift victories, he grew slack and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong pressed on to Yiyang; emboldened by his swift victories, he grew careless and made no defensive preparations.

sentences.zh: 九月，弘農太守垣延詐降，夜襲聰軍，聰大敗而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Yuan Yan, Administrator of Hongnong, feigned surrender and launched a night attack on Liu Cong's army; Liu Cong was badly defeated and retreated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Yuan Yan, Administrator of Hongnong, feigned surrender and launched a night attack on Liu Cong's army; Liu Cong suffered a crushing defeat and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 王浚遣祁弘與鮮卑段務勿塵擊石勒於飛龍山，大破之，勒退屯黎陽。

translations.literal: Wang Jun dispatched Qi Hong together with the Xianbei chief Duan Wuyuan to attack Shi Le at Feilong Mountain; they inflicted a great defeat, and Shi Le withdrew and encamped at Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun sent Qi Hong together with the Xianbei chief Duan Wuyuan to attack Shi Le at Feilong Mountain; they routed him, and Shi Le withdrew to encamp at Liyang.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢主淵復遣楚王聰、王彌、始安王曜、汝陰王景帥精騎五萬寇洛陽，大司空雁門剛穆公呼延翼帥步卒繼之。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, the Han ruler Liu Yuan again dispatched Prince of Chu Liu Cong, Wang Mi, Prince of Shi'an Liu Yao, and Prince of Ruyin Liu Jing leading fifty thousand elite cavalry to raid Luoyang; Grand Minister of Works Hu Yan of Yanmen, Duke Gangmu, followed with infantry.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Liu Yuan again sent Prince of Chu Liu Cong, Wang Mi, Prince of Shi'an Liu Yao, and Prince of Ruyin Liu Jing at the head of fifty thousand elite cavalry to raid Luoyang; Grand Minister of Works Huyan of Yanmen, Duke Gangmu, followed with infantry.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，聰等至宜陽。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Liu Cong and the others reached Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Liu Cong and the others reached Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以漢兵新敗，不意其復至，大懼。

translations.literal: The court, because Han forces had just been defeated, did not expect them to return so soon and was greatly alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: The court, having just seen Han forces defeated, did not expect them to return so soon and was gripped with fear.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，聰屯西明門。

translations.literal: On xinyou, Liu Cong encamped at the Ximing Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, Liu Cong encamped at the Ximing Gate.

sentences.zh: 北宮純等夜帥勇士千餘人出攻漢壁，斬其征虜將軍呼延顥。

translations.literal: Bei Gongchun and others by night led more than a thousand brave warriors out to attack the Han camp and killed their General Who Captures the Enemy Hu Yanhao.
translations.idiomatic: Bei Gongchun and others led more than a thousand warriors out by night to attack the Han camp and killed General Who Captures the Enemy Hu Yanhao.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，聰南屯洛水。

translations.literal: On renxu, Liu Cong encamped south of the Luo River.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Liu Cong encamped south of the Luo River.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，呼延翼為其下所殺，其眾自大陽潰歸。

translations.literal: On yichou, Hu Yan was killed by his own subordinates, and his troops fled in disorder from Dayang back home.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou, Huyan was killed by his own men, and his troops broke and fled from Dayang.

sentences.zh: 淵敕聰等還師。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan ordered Liu Cong and the others to withdraw their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan ordered Liu Cong and the others to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 聰表稱晉兵微弱，不可以翼、顥死故還師，固請留攻洛陽，淵許之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong submitted a memorial stating that Jin forces were weak and that the army should not withdraw merely because Hu Yan and Hu Yanhao had died; he firmly requested to remain and attack Luoyang, and Liu Yuan consented.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong submitted a memorial arguing that Jin forces were weak and that the army should not withdraw merely because Huyan and Hu Yanhao had died; he pressed to remain and attack Luoyang, and Liu Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 太傅越嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue closed the city and held it in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue shut himself inside the city and held it in defense.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，聰親祈嵩山，留平晉將軍安陽哀王厲、冠軍將軍呼延朗督攝留軍；

translations.literal: On wuyin, Liu Cong personally performed sacrifices on Mount Song; he left General Who Pacifies Jin Liu Li, Prince Ai of Anyang, and Champion General Hu Yanlang to oversee the remaining forces;
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin, Liu Cong personally performed sacrifices on Mount Song; he left General Who Pacifies Jin Liu Li, Prince Ai of Anyang, and Champion General Hu Yanlang in command of the remaining forces;

sentences.zh: 太傅參軍孫詢說越乘虛出擊朗，斬之，厲赴水死。

translations.literal: Sun Xun, a staff officer of the Grand Tutor, urged Sima Yue to seize the opportunity and strike Hu Yanlang; he was beheaded, and Liu Li drowned himself in the river.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xun, a staff officer of the Grand Tutor, urged Sima Yue to seize the moment and strike Hu Yanlang; Yanlang was beheaded, and Liu Li drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 王彌謂聰曰：「今軍既失利，洛陽守備猶固，運車在陝，糧食不支數日。

translations.literal: Wang Mi said to Liu Cong: "Now that our army has suffered setbacks, Luoyang's defenses remain strong; our supply wagons are at Shan, and our grain will not last more than a few days.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi told Liu Cong: "Our army has already suffered setbacks, Luoyang's defenses remain strong, our supply wagons are at Shan, and our grain will not last more than a few days.

sentences.zh: 殿下不如與龍驤還平陽，裹糧發卒，更為後舉；

translations.literal: Your Highness would do better to return to Pingyang with the Dragon Rapid Army, gather grain and raise troops, and mount a fresh campaign later;
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness would do better to return to Pingyang with the Dragon Rapid Army, gather grain, raise fresh troops, and mount a new campaign later;

sentences.zh: 下官亦收兵谷，待命於兗、豫，不亦可乎？」

translations.literal: I too will gather troops and grain and await orders in Yan and Yu—would that not also serve?"
translations.idiomatic: I will gather troops and grain as well and await your orders in Yan and Yu—would that not serve just as well?"

sentences.zh: 聰自以請留，未敢還。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, having himself requested to remain, did not dare withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, having himself pressed to remain, did not dare withdraw.

sentences.zh: 宣於修之言於淵曰：「歲在辛未，乃得洛陽。

translations.literal: Xuanyu Xiuzhi said to Liu Yuan: "In the year xinwei Luoyang will be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanyu Xiuzhi told Liu Yuan: "Only in the year xinwei will Luoyang be taken.

sentences.zh: 今晉氣猶盛，大軍不歸，必敗。」

translations.literal: Now Jin's vital energy is still strong; if the great army does not return, defeat is certain."
translations.idiomatic: Jin's fortunes are still strong; if the main army does not withdraw, it will surely be defeated."

sentences.zh: 淵乃召聰等還。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan thereupon summoned Liu Cong and the others back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan then recalled Liu Cong and the others.

sentences.zh: 天水人訇琦等殺成太尉李離、尚書令閻式，以梓潼降羅尚。

translations.literal: Hong Qi of Tianshui and others killed Cheng Grand Commandant Li Li and Director of the Masters of Writing Yan Shi, and surrendered Zitong to Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Hong Qi of Tianshui and others killed Li Li, Grand Commandant of Cheng, and Yan Shi, Director of the Masters of Writing, and surrendered Zitong to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 成主雄遣太傅驤、司徒雲、司空璜攻之，不克，雲、璜戰死。

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Li Xiong dispatched Grand Tutor Li Xiang, Minister over the Masses Li Yun, and Minister of Works Li Huang to attack them but failed; Li Yun and Li Huang died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong, ruler of Cheng, sent Grand Tutor Li Xiang, Minister over the Masses Li Yun, and Minister of Works Li Huang to attack them but failed; Li Yun and Li Huang were killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 初，譙周有子居巴西，成巴西太守馬脫殺之，其子登詣劉弘請兵以復仇。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qiao Zhou had a son living in Baxi; Ma Tuo, Administrator of Baxi under Cheng, killed him; his son Deng went to Liu Hong to request troops for revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qiao Zhou had a son living in Baxi; Ma Tuo, Cheng's Administrator of Baxi, killed him; the son Deng went to Liu Hong to request troops for revenge.

sentences.zh: 弘表登為梓潼內史，使自募巴、蜀流民，得二千人；

translations.literal: Liu Hong memorialized to appoint Deng Administrator of Zitong and had him recruit displaced people from Ba and Shu on his own, obtaining two thousand men;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong memorialized to appoint Deng Administrator of Zitong and had him recruit displaced people from Ba and Shu on his own, raising two thousand men;

sentences.zh: 西上，至巴郡，從羅尚求益兵，不得。

translations.literal: he marched west, reached Ba commandery, and asked Luo Shang for additional troops but received none.
translations.idiomatic: he marched west to Ba commandery and asked Luo Shang for reinforcements but received none.

sentences.zh: 登進攻宕渠，斬馬脫，食其肝。

translations.literal: Deng advanced to attack Dangqu, beheaded Ma Tuo, and ate his liver.
translations.idiomatic: Deng advanced against Dangqu, beheaded Ma Tuo, and ate his liver.

sentences.zh: 會梓潼降，登進據涪城；

translations.literal: When Zitong surrendered, Deng advanced and occupied Fucheng;
translations.idiomatic: When Zitong surrendered, Deng advanced and occupied Fucheng;

sentences.zh: 雄自攻之，為登所敗。

translations.literal: Li Xiong personally attacked him but was defeated by Deng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong personally attacked him but was defeated by Deng.

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲申，漢楚王聰、始安王曜歸於平陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, Han Prince of Chu Liu Cong and Prince of Shi'an Liu Yao returned to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiashen, Liu Cong, Prince of Chu of Han, and Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, returned to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 王彌南出轘轅，流民之在穎川、襄城、汝南、南陽、河南者數萬家，素為居民所苦，皆燒城邑，殺二千石、長吏以應彌。

translations.literal: Wang Mi marched south through Huanyuan; several tens of thousands of refugee households in Yingchuan, Xiangcheng, Runan, Nanyang, and Henan, long oppressed by the local residents, all burned cities and towns and killed grand administrators and chief officials to join Wang Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi marched south through Huanyuan; tens of thousands of refugee households in Yingchuan, Xiangcheng, Runan, Nanyang, and Henan, long oppressed by the local populace, burned cities and towns and killed grand administrators and chief officials to rally to Wang Mi.

sentences.zh: 石勒寇信都，殺冀州刺史王斌。

translations.literal: Shi Le raided Xindu and killed Inspector of Ji Province Wang Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le raided Xindu and killed Wang Bin, Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 王浚自領冀州。

translations.literal: Wang Jun personally assumed command of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun personally assumed command of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 詔車騎將軍王堪、北中郎將裴憲將兵討勒，勒引兵還，拒之；

translations.literal: An edict ordered General of Chariots and Cavalry Wang Kan and General of the North Central Guard Pei Xian to lead troops against Shi Le; Shi Le withdrew his army and resisted them;
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Wang Kan, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Pei Xian, General of the North Central Guard, to lead troops against Shi Le; Shi Le withdrew and resisted them;

sentences.zh: 魏郡太守劉矩以郡降勒。

translations.literal: Liu Ju, Administrator of Wei commandery, surrendered the commandery to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ju, Administrator of Wei commandery, surrendered the commandery to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 勒至黎陽，裴憲棄軍奔淮南，王堪退保倉垣。

translations.literal: When Shi Le reached Liyang, Pei Xian abandoned his army and fled to Huainan; Wang Kan withdrew to defend Cangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Le reached Liyang, Pei Xian abandoned his army and fled to Huainan; Wang Kan withdrew to hold Cangyuan.

sentences.zh: 十二月，漢主淵以陳留王歡樂為太傅，楚王聰為大司徒，江都王延年為大司空。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, the Han ruler Liu Yuan appointed Prince of Chenliu Liu Huanle Grand Tutor, Prince of Chu Liu Cong Grand Minister over the Masses, and Prince of Jiangdu Liu Yannian Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, Liu Yuan appointed Liu Huanle, Prince of Chenliu, Grand Tutor; Liu Cong, Prince of Chu, Grand Minister over the Masses; and Liu Yannian, Prince of Jiangdu, Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 遣都護大將軍曲陽王賢與征北大將軍劉靈、安北將軍趙固、平北將軍王桑，東屯內黃。

translations.literal: He dispatched Grand General Who Protects All Quyang Wang Liu Xian together with General Who Conquers the North Liu Ling, General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Gu, and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Sang to encamp east at Neihuang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Grand General Who Protects All Liu Xian, Prince of Quyang, together with General Who Conquers the North Liu Ling, General Who Pacifies the North Zhao Gu, and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Sang to encamp east at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 王彌表左長史曹嶷行安東將軍，東徇青州，且迎其家；

translations.literal: Wang Mi memorialized that his Left Chief Clerk Cao Ni should act as General Who Pacifies the East, sweep east through Qing Province, and also bring his family;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi memorialized that his Left Chief Clerk Cao Ni should serve as acting General Who Pacifies the East, sweep east through Qing Province, and also bring his family;

sentences.zh: 淵許之。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan consented.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan agreed.

sentences.zh: 初，東夷校尉勃海李臻，與王浚約共輔晉室，浚內有異志，臻恨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Zhen of Bohai, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, had agreed with Wang Jun to support the Jin house together; Wang Jun harbored disloyal ambitions within, and Li Zhen resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Zhen of Bohai, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, had agreed with Wang Jun to support the Jin house together; Wang Jun harbored disloyal ambitions of his own, and Li Zhen resented him.

sentences.zh: 和演之死也，別駕昌黎王誕亡歸李臻，說臻舉兵討浚。

translations.literal: When He Yan died, Assistant Administrator Wang Dan of Changli fled to Li Zhen and urged him to raise troops to punish Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: When He Yan died, Wang Dan of Changli, Assistant Administrator, fled to Li Zhen and urged him to raise troops against Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 臻遣其子成將兵擊浚。

translations.literal: Li Zhen dispatched his son Li Cheng with troops to attack Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhen sent his son Li Cheng with troops to attack Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 遼東太守龐本，素與臻有隙，乘虛襲殺臻，遣人殺成於無慮。

translations.literal: Pang Ben, Administrator of Liaodong, had long been at odds with Li Zhen; seizing the opportunity he launched a surprise attack and killed Li Zhen, and sent men to kill Li Cheng at Wulu.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Ben, Administrator of Liaodong, had long been at odds with Li Zhen; seizing the opportunity he launched a surprise attack and killed Li Zhen, and sent men to kill Li Cheng at Wulu.

sentences.zh: 誕亡歸慕容廆。

translations.literal: Wang Dan fled and submitted to Murong Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dan fled and submitted to Murong Hui.

sentences.zh: 詔以勃海封釋代臻為東夷校尉，龐本復謀殺之；

translations.literal: An edict appointed Feng Shi of Bohai to replace Li Zhen as Colonel of the Eastern Yi; Pang Ben again plotted to kill him;
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Feng Shi of Bohai to replace Li Zhen as Colonel of the Eastern Yi; Pang Ben again plotted to kill him;

sentences.zh: 釋子悛勸釋伏兵請本，收斬之，悉誅其家。

translations.literal: Feng Shi's son Feng Jun urged Feng Shi to set an ambush and invite Pang Ben, seize and behead him, and execute his entire family.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shi's son Feng Jun urged Feng Shi to set an ambush, invite Pang Ben in, seize and behead him, and execute his entire family.

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝中永嘉四年（

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part, Yongjia Year Four (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part—Yongjia, Year Four (

sentences.zh: 庚午，公元三一零年）

translations.literal: gengwu, CE 310)
translations.idiomatic: gengwu, 310 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，乙丑朔，大赦。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on the first day yichou, a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on the new moon of yichou, a general amnesty was declared.

sentences.zh: 漢主淵立單征女為皇后，梁王和為皇太子，大赦；

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Yuan installed the daughter of Shan Zheng as empress, Prince of Liang Liu He as crown prince, and proclaimed a general amnesty;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yuan installed the daughter of Shan Zheng as empress, made Liu He, Prince of Liang, crown prince, and declared a general amnesty;

sentences.zh: 封子義為北海王；

translations.literal: he enfeoffed his son Liu Yi as Prince of Beihai;
translations.idiomatic: he enfeoffed his son Liu Yi as Prince of Beihai;

sentences.zh: 以長樂王洋為大司馬。

translations.literal: he appointed Prince of Changle Liu Yang Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: and appointed Liu Yang, Prince of Changle, Grand Marshal.

sentences.zh: 漢鎮東大將軍石勒濟河，拔白馬，王彌以三萬眾會之，共寇徐、豫、兗州。

translations.literal: Han General Who Pacifies the East Shi Le crossed the river, captured Baima, and Wang Mi joined him with thirty thousand men; together they raided Xu, Yu, and Yan provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le, Han General Who Pacifies the East, crossed the river, captured Baima, and Wang Mi joined him with thirty thousand men; together they raided Xu, Yu, and Yan provinces.

sentences.zh: 二月，勒襲鄄城，殺兗州刺史袁孚，遂拔倉垣，殺王堪。

translations.literal: In the second month, Shi Le raided Juancheng, killed Inspector of Yan Province Yuan Fu, then captured Cangyuan and killed Wang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Shi Le raided Juancheng, killed Yuan Fu, Inspector of Yan Province, then captured Cangyuan and killed Wang Kan.

sentences.zh: 復北濟河，攻冀州諸郡，民從之者九萬餘口。

translations.literal: He again crossed the river northward and attacked the commanderies of Ji Province; more than ninety thousand people followed him.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river north again and attacked the commanderies of Ji Province; more than ninety thousand people followed him.

sentences.zh: 成太尉李國鎮巴西，帳下文石殺國，以巴西降羅尚。

translations.literal: Li Guo, Cheng Grand Commandant, was stationed in Baxi; Wen Shi, a clerk in his staff, killed Li Guo and surrendered Baxi to Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guo, Cheng Grand Commandant, was stationed in Baxi; Wen Shi, a clerk on his staff, killed Li Guo and surrendered Baxi to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 太傅越征建威將軍吳興錢璯及揚州刺史王敦。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue summoned Jianwei General Qian Kai of Wuxing and Inspector of Yang Province Wang Dun.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue summoned Qian Kai of Wuxing, Jianwei General, and Wang Dun, Inspector of Yang Province.

sentences.zh: 璯謀殺敦以反，敦奔建業，告琅邪王睿。

translations.literal: Qian Kai plotted to kill Wang Dun and rebel; Wang Dun fled to Jianye and reported the matter to Prince of Langya Sima Rui.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Kai plotted to kill Wang Dun and rebel; Wang Dun fled to Jianye and reported the matter to Sima Rui, Prince of Langya.

sentences.zh: 璯遂反，進寇陽羨，睿遣將軍郭逸等討之；

translations.literal: Qian Kai then rebelled and advanced to raid Yangxian; Sima Rui dispatched General Guo Yi and others to suppress him;
translations.idiomatic: Qian Kai then rebelled and advanced to raid Yangxian; Sima Rui sent General Guo Yi and others to suppress him;

sentences.zh: 周□糾合鄉里，與逸等共討璯，斬之。

translations.literal: Zhou Ji organized his fellow townspeople and joined Guo Yi and the others in attacking Qian Kai, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Ji rallied his fellow townspeople and joined Guo Yi and the others in attacking Qian Kai, killing him.

sentences.zh: □三定江南，睿以□為吳興太守，於其鄉里置義興郡以旌之。

translations.literal: Ji three times stabilized Jiangnan; Sima Rui appointed Ji Administrator of Wuxing and established Yixing commandery in his hometown to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: This was Ji's third pacification of Jiangnan; Sima Rui appointed Ji Administrator of Wuxing and established Yixing commandery in his hometown to honor him.

sentences.zh: 曹嶷自大梁引兵而東，所至皆下，遂克東平，進攻琅邪。

translations.literal: Cao Ni led troops east from Daliang; wherever he went all submitted, and he captured Dongping and advanced to attack Langya.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Ni led troops east from Daliang; wherever he went all submitted; he captured Dongping and advanced to attack Langya.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，王浚將祁弘敗漢冀州刺史劉靈於廣宗，殺之。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Qi Hong, a general of Wang Jun, defeated Han Inspector of Ji Province Liu Ling at Guangzong and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Qi Hong, a general under Wang Jun, defeated Liu Ling, Han Inspector of Ji Province, at Guangzong and killed him.

sentences.zh: 成主雄謂其將張寶曰：「汝能得梓潼，吾以李離之官賞汝。」

translations.literal: Cheng ruler Li Xiong said to his general Zhang Bao: "If you can take Zitong, I will reward you with Li Li's office."
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong, ruler of Cheng, told his general Zhang Bao: "If you can take Zitong, I will reward you with Li Li's office."

sentences.zh: 寶乃先殺人而亡奔梓潼，訇琦等信之，委以心腹。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao then first killed someone and fled to Zitong; Hong Qi and the others trusted him and entrusted him as a close confidant.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao then killed someone and fled to Zitong; Hong Qi and the others trusted him and made him a close confidant.

sentences.zh: 會羅尚遣使至梓潼，琦等出送之；

translations.literal: When Luo Shang dispatched envoys to Zitong, Hong Qi and the others went out to escort them;
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Shang sent envoys to Zitong, Hong Qi and the others went out to escort them;

sentences.zh: 寶從後閉門，琦等奔巴西。

translations.literal: Zhang Bao closed the gates from behind; Hong Qi and the others fled to Baxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bao closed the gates behind them; Hong Qi and the others fled to Baxi.

sentences.zh: 雄以寶為太尉。

translations.literal: Li Xiong appointed Zhang Bao Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong appointed Zhang Bao Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 幽、并、司、冀、秦、雍六州大蝗，食草木、牛馬毛皆盡。

translations.literal: In the six provinces of You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong a great locust plague occurred; they devoured grass and trees and even the hair of cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: A great locust plague struck the six provinces of You, Bing, Si, Ji, Qin, and Yong; the locusts devoured grass and trees and even stripped the hair from cattle and horses.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，漢楚王聰、始安王曜、石勒及安北大將軍越國圍河內太守裴整於懷，詔征虜將軍宋抽救懷。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Han Prince of Chu Liu Cong, Prince of Shi'an Liu Yao, Shi Le, and General Who Pacifies the North Yue Guo besieged Pei Zheng, Administrator of Henei, at Huai; an edict ordered General Who Captures the Enemy Song Chou to rescue Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Liu Cong, Prince of Chu of Han, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, Shi Le, and General Who Pacifies the North Yue Guo besieged Pei Zheng, Administrator of Henei, at Huai; an edict ordered Song Chou, General Who Captures the Enemy, to rescue Huai.

sentences.zh: 勒與平北大將軍王桑逆擊抽，殺之；

translations.literal: Shi Le and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Sang intercepted and attacked Song Chou, killing him;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le and General Who Pacifies the North Wang Sang intercepted Song Chou and killed him;

sentences.zh: 河內人執整以降，漢主淵以整為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: the people of Henei seized Pei Zheng and surrendered; the Han ruler Liu Yuan appointed Pei Zheng Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: the people of Henei seized Pei Zheng and surrendered; Liu Yuan appointed Pei Zheng Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 河內督將郭默收整餘眾，自為塢主，劉琨以默為河內太守。

translations.literal: Guo Mo, a garrison commander of Henei, gathered Pei Zheng's remaining troops and made himself master of a fortified settlement; Liu Kun appointed Guo Mo Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Mo, a garrison commander of Henei, gathered Pei Zheng's remaining troops and made himself master of a fortified settlement; Liu Kun appointed Guo Mo Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 羅尚卒於巴郡，詔以長沙太守下邳皮素代之。

translations.literal: Luo Shang died in Ba commandery; an edict appointed Pi Su of Xiapi, Administrator of Changsha, to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang died in Ba commandery; an edict appointed Pi Su of Xiapi, Administrator of Changsha, to replace him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，漢主淵寢疾；

translations.literal: On gengwu, the Han ruler Liu Yuan fell gravely ill;
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Liu Yuan fell gravely ill;

sentences.zh: 辛未，以陳留王歡樂為太宰，長樂王洋為太傅，江都王延年為太保，楚王聰為大司馬、大單于，並錄尚書事。

translations.literal: On xinwei, Prince of Chenliu Liu Huanle was appointed Grand Preceptor, Prince of Changle Liu Yang Grand Tutor, Prince of Jiangdu Liu Yannian Grand Protector, and Prince of Chu Liu Cong Grand Marshal and Grand Chanyu, all with concurrent charge of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei, Liu Huanle, Prince of Chenliu, was appointed Grand Preceptor; Liu Yang, Prince of Changle, Grand Tutor; Liu Yannian, Prince of Jiangdu, Grand Protector; and Liu Cong, Prince of Chu, Grand Marshal and Grand Chanyu—all with concurrent charge of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 置單于台於平陽西。

translations.literal: The Chanyu Platform was established west of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu Platform was established west of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 以齊王裕為大司徒，魯王隆為尚書令，北海王乂為撫軍大將軍、領司隸校尉，始安王曜為征討大都督、領單于左輔，廷尉喬智明為冠軍大將軍、領單于右輔，光祿大夫劉殷為左僕射，王育為右僕射，任顗為吏部尚書，朱紀為中書監，護軍馬景領左衛將軍，永安王安國領右衛將軍，安昌王盛、安邑王飲、西陽王璿皆領武衛將軍，分典禁兵。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Liu Yu was appointed Grand Minister over the Masses; Prince of Lu Liu Long, Director of the Masters of Writing; Prince of Beihai Liu Yi, General Who Pacifies the Army with concurrent charge as Colonel of the Metropolitan Area; Prince of Shi'an Liu Yao, Grand Commander-in-Chief for Campaigns with concurrent charge as Left Assistant Chanyu; Qiao Zhiming, Minister of Justice, Champion General with concurrent charge as Right Assistant Chanyu; Liu Yin, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Vice Director; Wang Yu, Right Vice Director; Ren Yi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Zhu Ji, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; Protector of the Army Ma Jing, acting Left Guard General; Prince of Yong'an Liu Anguo, acting Right Guard General; Prince of Anchang Liu Sheng, Prince of Anyi Liu Yin, and Prince of Xiyang Liu Xuan all acting Generals of Martial Guard, each commanding a portion of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu, Prince of Qi, was made Grand Minister over the Masses; Liu Long, Prince of Lu, Director of the Masters of Writing; Liu Yi, Prince of Beihai, General Who Pacifies the Army with concurrent charge as Colonel of the Metropolitan Area; Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, Grand Commander-in-Chief for Campaigns with concurrent charge as Left Assistant Chanyu; Qiao Zhiming, Minister of Justice, Champion General with concurrent charge as Right Assistant Chanyu; Liu Yin, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, Left Vice Director; Wang Yu, Right Vice Director; Ren Yi, Director of the Ministry of Personnel; Zhu Ji, Supervisor of the Masters of Writing; Protector of the Army Ma Jing, acting Left Guard General; Liu Anguo, Prince of Yong'an, acting Right Guard General; and Liu Sheng, Prince of Anchang, Liu Yin, Prince of Anyi, and Liu Xuan, Prince of Xiyang, all acting Generals of Martial Guard, each commanding a portion of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 初，盛少時，不好讀書，唯讀《孝經》、《論語》，曰：「誦此能行，足矣，安用多誦而不行乎！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when Liu Sheng was young he did not love reading; he read only the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, saying: "If one can recite these and act on them, that is enough—what use is much reciting without acting!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Liu Sheng was young he did not love reading; he read only the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects, saying: "If one can recite these and live by them, that is enough—what use is reciting much without acting!"

sentences.zh: 李熹見之，歎曰：「望之如可易，及至，肅如嚴君，可謂君子矣！」

translations.literal: When Li Xi saw him, he sighed and said: "At a distance he seems easy to approach, but up close he is as stern as a strict lord—he may truly be called a gentleman!"
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xi saw him, he sighed and said: "At a distance he seems easy to approach, but up close he is as stern as a strict lord—he may truly be called a gentleman!"

sentences.zh: 淵以其忠篤，故臨終委以要任。

translations.literal: Liu Yuan, because of his loyalty and steadfastness, therefore on his deathbed entrusted him with a crucial post.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his loyalty and steadfastness, Liu Yuan entrusted him with a crucial post on his deathbed.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，淵召太宰歡樂等入禁中，受遺詔輔政。

translations.literal: On dingchou, Liu Yuan summoned Grand Preceptor Liu Huanle and the others into the inner palace to receive the deathbed edict and assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Liu Yuan summoned Grand Preceptor Liu Huanle and the others into the inner palace to receive the deathbed edict and assist in government.

sentences.zh: 己卯，淵卒；

translations.literal: On jimao, Liu Yuan died;
translations.idiomatic: On jimao, Liu Yuan died;

sentences.zh: 太子和即位。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Liu He ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Liu He ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 和性猜忌無恩。

translations.literal: Liu He was by nature suspicious and devoid of kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He was by nature suspicious and devoid of kindness.

sentences.zh: 宗正呼延攸，翼之子也，淵以其無才行，終身不遷官；

translations.literal: Director of the Imperial Clan Huyan You, son of Hu Yan, because Liu Yuan considered him lacking in ability and conduct, was never promoted throughout his life;
translations.idiomatic: Huyan You, Director of the Imperial Clan and son of Huyan, because Liu Yuan considered him lacking in ability and conduct, was never promoted throughout his life;

sentences.zh: 侍中劉乘，素惡楚王聰；

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Liu Cheng had long hated Prince of Chu Liu Cong;
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Liu Cheng had long hated Liu Cong, Prince of Chu;

sentences.zh: 衛尉西昌王銳，恥不預顧命；

translations.literal: Commandant of the Guards Liu Rui, Prince of Xichang, was shamed at not being included in the deathbed appointment;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui, Prince of Xichang, Commandant of the Guards, was shamed at not being included in the deathbed appointment;

sentences.zh: 乃相與謀，說和曰：「先帝不惟輕重之勢，使三王總強兵於內，大司馬擁十萬眾屯於近郊，陛下便為寄坐耳。

translations.literal: they therefore plotted together and said to Liu He: "The late emperor, without regard for the balance of power, left three princes commanding strong armies within the palace, and the Grand Marshal holding one hundred thousand men encamped in the near suburbs—you, Your Majesty, are but a figurehead.
translations.idiomatic: they therefore plotted together and told Liu He: "The late emperor, without regard for the balance of power, left three princes commanding strong armies within the palace, and the Grand Marshal holding one hundred thousand men encamped in the near suburbs—you, Your Majesty, are but a figurehead.

sentences.zh: 宜早為之計。」

translations.literal: You should plan early."
translations.idiomatic: You should act early."

sentences.zh: 和，攸之甥也，深信之。

translations.literal: Liu He, being Huyan You's nephew, trusted him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He, being Huyan You's nephew, trusted him completely.

sentences.zh: 辛巳夜，召安昌王盛、安邑王欽等告之。

translations.literal: On the night of xinsi, he summoned Prince of Anchang Liu Sheng, Prince of Anyi Liu Qin, and the others and told them.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of xinsi, he summoned Liu Sheng, Prince of Anchang, Liu Qin, Prince of Anyi, and the others and told them.

sentences.zh: 盛曰：「先帝梓宮在殯，四王未有逆節，一旦自相魚肉，天下謂陛下何！

translations.literal: Liu Sheng said: "The late emperor's coffin is still in mourning; the four princes have shown no disloyalty—if we suddenly turn on one another, what will the realm think of Your Majesty!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Sheng said: "The late emperor's coffin is still in mourning; the four princes have shown no disloyalty—if we suddenly turn on one another, what will the realm think of Your Majesty!

sentences.zh: 且大業甫爾，陛下勿信讒夫之言以疑兄弟。

translations.literal: Moreover, the great enterprise has only just begun—Your Majesty must not believe slanderers' words and grow suspicious of your brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the great enterprise has only just begun—Your Majesty must not believe slanderers and grow suspicious of your brothers.

sentences.zh: 兄弟尚不可信，他人誰足信哉！」

translations.literal: If even brothers cannot be trusted, who else is worth trusting!"
translations.idiomatic: If even brothers cannot be trusted, who else is worth trusting!"

sentences.zh: 攸、銳怒之曰：「今日之議，理無有二，領軍是何言乎！」

translations.literal: Huyan You and Liu Rui said angrily: "In today's deliberations there can be no two views—what talk is this from the commander of the guard!"
translations.idiomatic: Huyan You and Liu Rui said angrily: "In today's deliberations there can be no two views—what talk is this from the commander of the guard!"

sentences.zh: 命左右刃之。

translations.literal: He ordered those at his side to cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered those at his side to cut him down.

sentences.zh: 盛既死，欽懼曰：「惟陛下命！」

translations.literal: After Liu Sheng was dead, Liu Qin said in fear: "I await Your Majesty's command!"
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Sheng was dead, Liu Qin said in fear: "I await Your Majesty's command!"

sentences.zh: 壬午，銳帥馬景攻楚王聰於單于台，攸帥永安王安國攻齊王裕於司徒府，乘帥安邑王飲攻魯王隆，使尚書田密、武衛將軍劉璿攻北海王乂。

translations.literal: On renwu, Liu Rui led Ma Jing to attack Prince of Chu Liu Cong at the Chanyu Platform; Huyan You led Prince of Yong'an Liu Anguo to attack Prince of Qi Liu Yu at the Minister over the Masses' office; Liu Cheng led Prince of Anyi Liu Yin to attack Prince of Lu Liu Long; and he had Masters of Writing Tian Mi and General of Martial Guard Liu Xuan attack Prince of Beihai Liu Yi.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, Liu Rui led Ma Jing to attack Liu Cong, Prince of Chu, at the Chanyu Platform; Huyan You led Liu Anguo, Prince of Yong'an, to attack Liu Yu, Prince of Qi, at the Minister over the Masses' office; Liu Cheng led Liu Yin, Prince of Anyi, to attack Liu Long, Prince of Lu; and he had Tian Mi of the Masters of Writing and Liu Xuan, General of Martial Guard, attack Liu Yi, Prince of Beihai.

sentences.zh: 密、璿挾乂斬關歸於聰，聰命貫甲以待之。

translations.literal: Tian Mi and Liu Xuan seized Liu Yi, broke through the gate, and returned to Liu Cong; Liu Cong ordered his men to don armor and await them.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Mi and Liu Xuan seized Liu Yi, broke through the gate, and returned to Liu Cong; Liu Cong ordered his men to don armor and await them.

sentences.zh: 銳知聰有備，馳還，與攸、乘共攻隆、裕。

translations.literal: Liu Rui, knowing Liu Cong was prepared, galloped back and joined Huyan You and Liu Cheng in attacking Liu Long and Liu Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui, knowing Liu Cong was prepared, galloped back and joined Huyan You and Liu Cheng in attacking Liu Long and Liu Yu.

sentences.zh: 攸、乘疑安國、欽有異志，殺之。

translations.literal: Huyan You and Liu Cheng suspected Liu Anguo and Liu Qin of disloyal intentions and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huyan You and Liu Cheng suspected Liu Anguo and Liu Qin of disloyal intentions and killed them.

sentences.zh: 是日，斬裕，癸未，斬隆。

translations.literal: That day Liu Yu was beheaded; on guiwei Liu Long was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: That day Liu Yu was beheaded; on guiwei Liu Long was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 甲申，聰攻西明門，克之；

translations.literal: On jiashen, Liu Cong attacked the Ximing Gate and captured it;
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Liu Cong attacked the Ximing Gate and captured it;

sentences.zh: 銳等走入南宮，前鋒隨之。

translations.literal: Liu Rui and the others fled into the Southern Palace, and the vanguard followed after them.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rui and the others fled into the Southern Palace, and the vanguard followed after them.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，殺和於光極西室，收銳、攸、乘，梟首通衢。

translations.literal: On yiyou, Liu He was killed in the Western Chamber of the Hall of Light; Liu Rui, Huyan You, and Liu Cheng were seized and their heads displayed on the public thoroughfare.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou, Liu He was killed in the Western Chamber of the Hall of Light; Liu Rui, Huyan You, and Liu Cheng were seized and their heads displayed on the public thoroughfare.

sentences.zh: 群臣請聰即帝位；

translations.literal: The ministers requested that Liu Cong ascend the imperial throne;
translations.idiomatic: The ministers urged Liu Cong to ascend the imperial throne;

sentences.zh: 聰以北海王乂，單後之子也，以位讓之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong, because Prince of Beihai Liu Yi was the son of Empress Shan, offered the throne to him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, because Liu Yi, Prince of Beihai, was the son of Empress Shan, offered the throne to him.

sentences.zh: 乂涕泣固請，聰久而許之，曰：「乂及群公正以禍難尚殷，貪孤年長故耳。

translations.literal: Liu Yi wept and firmly declined; after a long while Liu Cong consented and said: "Yi and the ministers are yielding to me only because calamity still presses close and because they favor my greater age.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi wept and firmly declined; after a long while Liu Cong consented and said: "Yi and the ministers are yielding to me only because calamity still presses close and because they favor my greater age.

sentences.zh: 此家國之事，孤何敢辭！

translations.literal: This is a matter of the state and the house—how dare I decline!
translations.idiomatic: This is a matter of state and dynasty—how dare I decline!

sentences.zh: 俟乂年長，當以大業歸之。」

translations.literal: When Yi comes of age, the great enterprise shall be returned to him."
translations.idiomatic: When Yi comes of age, the great enterprise shall be returned to him."

sentences.zh: 遂即位。

translations.literal: He thereupon ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元光興。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, and the era name was changed to Guangxing.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was declared, and the era name was changed to Guangxing.

sentences.zh: 尊單氏曰皇太后，其母張氏曰帝太后。

translations.literal: Lady Shan was honored as Empress Dowager, and his mother Lady Zhang as Imperial Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shan was honored as Empress Dowager, and his mother Lady Zhang as Imperial Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以義為皇太弟、領大單于、大司徒。

translations.literal: Liu Yi was appointed Imperial Younger Brother, with concurrent charge as Grand Chanyu and Grand Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi was appointed Imperial Younger Brother, with concurrent charge as Grand Chanyu and Grand Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 立其妻呼延氏為皇后。

translations.literal: His wife Lady Huyan was installed as empress.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Lady Huyan was installed as empress.

sentences.zh: 呼延氏，淵後之從父妹也。

translations.literal: Lady Huyan was a paternal cousin of Liu Yuan's empress.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huyan was a paternal cousin of Liu Yuan's empress.

sentences.zh: 封其子粲為河內王，易為河間王，翼為彭城王，悝為高平王；

translations.literal: He enfeoffed his sons: Liu Can as Prince of Henei, Liu Yi as Prince of Hejian, Liu Yi as Prince of Pengcheng, and Liu Ti as Prince of Gaoping;
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed his sons—Liu Can as Prince of Henei, Liu Yi as Prince of Hejian, Liu Yi as Prince of Pengcheng, and Liu Ti as Prince of Gaoping;

sentences.zh: 仍以粲為撫軍大將軍、都督中外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Liu Can was further appointed General Who Stabilizes the Army and Supervisor of All Military Affairs at court and in the field.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can was also made General Who Stabilizes the Army and given overall command of all military affairs.

sentences.zh: 以石勒為并州刺史，封汲郡公。

translations.literal: Shi Le was appointed Inspector of Bing Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le was made Inspector of Bing Province and enfeoffed as Duke of Ji.

sentences.zh: 略陽臨渭氐酋蒲洪，驍勇多權略，群氐畏服之。

translations.literal: Pu Hong, chieftain of the Di at Linwei in Lueyang, was fierce and brave and full of stratagems; all the Di feared and submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Pu Hong, chieftain of the Di at Linwei in Lueyang, was a fierce fighter and cunning tactician whom the Di tribes feared and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰遣使拜洪平遠將軍，洪不受，自稱護氐校尉、秦州刺史、略陽公。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Cong dispatched envoys to appoint Hong General Who Pacifies the Distance; Hong did not accept, and styled himself Protector of the Di Colonel, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, ruler of Han, sent envoys to appoint Pu Hong General Who Pacifies the Distance, but Hong refused and styled himself Protector of the Di, Inspector of Qin Province, and Duke of Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 九月，辛未，葬漢主淵於永光陵，謚曰光文皇帝，廟號高祖。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on xinwei, the Han ruler Liu Yuan was buried at Yongguang Mausoleum; his posthumous title was Emperor Guangwen, and his temple name was Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on xinwei, Liu Yuan, ruler of Han, was buried at Yongguang Mausoleum with the posthumous title Emperor Guangwen and the temple name Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 雍州流民多在南陽，詔書遣還鄉里。

translations.literal: Many displaced persons from Yong Province were in Nanyang; an imperial edict ordered them sent back to their native districts.
translations.idiomatic: Many refugees from Yong Province had settled in Nanyang, and an imperial edict ordered them sent home.

sentences.zh: 流民以關中荒殘，皆不願歸；

translations.literal: The displaced persons, because Guanzhong was desolate and ruined, all were unwilling to return;
translations.idiomatic: The refugees, finding Guanzhong desolate and ruined, were unwilling to go back;

sentences.zh: 征南將軍山簡、南中郎將杜蕤各遣兵送之，促期令發。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian and Southern Central Commandant Du Rui each dispatched troops to escort them and set a deadline for departure.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian and Southern Central Commandant Du Rui each sent troops to escort them home and set a firm deadline for departure.

sentences.zh: 京兆王如遂潛結壯士，夜襲二軍，破之。

translations.literal: Wang Ru of Jingzhao thereupon secretly gathered stalwart men and by night attacked the two armies, defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru of Jingzhao secretly rallied fighting men and launched a night attack on the two armies, routing them.

sentences.zh: 於是馮翊嚴嶷、京兆侯脫各聚眾攻城鎮，殺令長以應之，未幾，眾至四五萬，自號大將軍、領司、雍二州牧，稱籓於漢。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yan Ni of Fengyi and Hou Tuo of Jingzhao each gathered multitudes, attacked walled towns, and killed magistrates in response; before long their forces reached forty or fifty thousand; they styled themselves Grand General and concurrent Governors of the two provinces of Si and Yong, and declared themselves tributaries to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ni of Fengyi and Hou Tuo of Jingzhao then raised armies, stormed garrison towns, and killed local officials in support; within a short time their forces swelled to forty or fifty thousand. They styled themselves Grand General and Governors of Si and Yong and acknowledged Han as their suzerain.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，漢河內王粲、始安王曜及王彌帥眾四萬寇洛陽，石勒帥騎二萬會粲於大陽，敗監軍裴邈於澠池，遂長驅入洛川。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Liu Can, Prince of Henei of Han, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, and Wang Mi led forty thousand men to raid Luoyang; Shi Le led twenty thousand horsemen to join Liu Can at Dayang, defeated Overseer Pei Miao at Mianchi, and then drove deep into the Luoyang region.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Liu Can, Prince of Henei, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, and Wang Mi led forty thousand men against Luoyang. Shi Le brought twenty thousand cavalry to join Liu Can at Dayang, defeated Overseer Pei Miao at Mianchi, and swept deep into the Luoyang basin.

sentences.zh: 粲出軒轅，掠梁、陳、汝、穎間。

translations.literal: Liu Can issued forth by Xuanyuan Pass and plundered the regions between Liang, Chen, Ru, and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Can marched out through Xuanyuan Pass and ravaged the lands between Liang, Chen, Ru, and Ying.

sentences.zh: 勒出成皋關，壬寅，圍陳留太守王贊於倉垣，為贊所敗，退屯文石津。

translations.literal: Shi Le issued forth by Chenggao Pass; on renyin he besieged Wang Zan, Administrator of Chenliu, at Cangyuan, was defeated by Wang Zan, and withdrew to encamp at Wenshi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marched out through Chenggao Pass; on renyin he besieged Wang Zan, Administrator of Chenliu, at Cangyuan, was beaten back, and withdrew to Wenshi Ford.

sentences.zh: 劉琨自將討劉虎及白部，遣使卑辭厚禮說鮮卑拓跋猗盧以請兵。

translations.literal: Liu Kun personally led troops to attack Liu Hu and the Bai tribe; he dispatched envoys with humble words and rich gifts to persuade the Xianbei chieftain Tuoba Yilu to lend troops.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun personally took the field against Liu Hu and the Bai tribe and sent envoys with humble words and lavish gifts to persuade the Xianbei chieftain Tuoba Yilu to send troops.

sentences.zh: 猗盧使其弟弗之子鬱律帥騎二萬助之，遂破劉虎、白部，屠其營。

translations.literal: Tuoba Yilu had his younger brother Fu's son Yulü lead twenty thousand horsemen to assist him; they thereupon defeated Liu Hu and the Bai tribe and slaughtered their camps.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Yilu sent his nephew Yulü, son of his younger brother Fu, at the head of twenty thousand cavalry to help; together they routed Liu Hu and the Bai tribe and wiped out their camps.

sentences.zh: 琨與猗盧結為兄弟，表猗盧為大單于，以代郡封之為代公。

translations.literal: Liu Kun and Tuoba Yilu entered into brotherhood; he memorialized Tuoba Yilu as Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai with Dai commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun and Tuoba Yilu swore brotherhood; he memorialized the court to make Tuoba Yilu Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai, granting him Dai commandery.

sentences.zh: 時代郡屬幽州，王浚不許，遣兵擊猗盧，猗盧拒破之。

translations.literal: At that time Dai commandery belonged to You Province; Wang Jun would not permit it and dispatched troops to attack Tuoba Yilu; Tuoba Yilu resisted and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Dai commandery then fell under You Province, and Wang Jun refused to accept the arrangement; he sent troops against Tuoba Yilu, who fought them off and won.

sentences.zh: 浚由是與琨有隙。

translations.literal: Wang Jun thereby came to have a rift with Liu Kun.
translations.idiomatic: From this Wang Jun and Liu Kun became estranged.

sentences.zh: 猗盧以封邑去國懸遠，民不相接，乃帥部落萬餘家自雲中入雁門，從琨求陘北之地。

translations.literal: Tuoba Yilu, because his enfeoffment was far from his homeland and the people were not contiguous, thereupon led more than ten thousand households of his tribes from Yunzhong into Yanmen and requested from Liu Kun the lands north of Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Yilu found his new fief too far from his homeland for his people to remain connected, so he led more than ten thousand tribal households from Yunzhong into Yanmen and asked Liu Kun for the lands north of Xing Pass.

sentences.zh: 琨不能制，且欲倚之為援，乃徙樓煩、馬邑、陰館、繁畤、崞五縣民於陘南，以其地與猗盧；

translations.literal: Liu Kun could not control him and moreover wished to rely on him as support; he thereupon moved the people of the five counties of Loufan, Mayi, Yinguan, Fanzhi, and Guo south of Xing and gave the land to Tuoba Yilu;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun could not restrain him and hoped to use him as an ally, so he relocated the people of Loufan, Mayi, Yinguan, Fanzhi, and Guo to the south of Xing Pass and ceded the territory to Tuoba Yilu;

sentences.zh: 由是猗盧益盛。

translations.literal: Thereby Tuoba Yilu grew ever stronger.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Yilu grew stronger still.

sentences.zh: 琨遣使言於太傅越，請出兵共討劉聰、石勒；

translations.literal: Liu Kun dispatched envoys to speak to Grand Tutor Sima Yue, requesting that troops be sent out jointly to attack Liu Cong and Shi Le;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun sent envoys to Grand Tutor Sima Yue asking for a joint campaign against Liu Cong and Shi Le;

sentences.zh: 越忌苟晞及豫州刺史馮嵩，恐為後患，不許。

translations.literal: Sima Yue was jealous of Gou Xi and Feng Song, Inspector of Yu Province, fearing they would become a later trouble, and did not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue distrusted Gou Xi and Feng Song, Inspector of Yu Province, fearing future trouble from them, and refused.

sentences.zh: 琨乃謝猗盧之兵，遣歸國。

translations.literal: Liu Kun thereupon thanked Tuoba Yilu for his troops and sent them back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun then thanked Tuoba Yilu for his aid and sent the troops home.

sentences.zh: 劉虎收餘眾，西渡河，居朔方肆盧川，漢主聰以虎宗室，封樓煩公。

translations.literal: Liu Hu gathered the remnant forces, crossed the river westward, and dwelt at Silu River in Shuofang; the Han ruler Liu Cong, because Hu was of the imperial clan, enfeoffed him as Duke of Loufan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu rallied the survivors, crossed west over the river, and settled on the Silu River in Shuofang; Liu Cong, ruler of Han, enfeoffed him as Duke of Loufan because he was a member of the imperial clan.

sentences.zh: 壬子，以劉琨為平北大將軍，王浚為司空，進鮮卑段務勿塵為大單于。

translations.literal: On renzi, Liu Kun was appointed General Who Pacifies the North, Wang Jun was appointed Minister of Works, and the Xianbei chieftain Duan Wuyuan was promoted to Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Liu Kun was made General Who Pacifies the North, Wang Jun was appointed Minister of Works, and the Xianbei chieftain Duan Wuyuan was promoted to Grand Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 京師饑困日甚，太傅越遣使以羽檄征天下兵，使入援京師。

translations.literal: Hunger and distress in the capital grew daily worse; Grand Tutor Sima Yue dispatched envoys with urgent summons to levy troops throughout the realm and have them enter to rescue the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and hardship in the capital worsened by the day; Grand Tutor Sima Yue sent urgent summons throughout the realm calling for troops to march to the capital's relief.

sentences.zh: 帝謂使者曰：「為我語諸征、鎮：今日尚可救，後則無及矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said to the envoy: "Speak for me to the regional commanders and territorial governors: today we can still be saved; afterward it will be too late!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told the envoy: "Tell the regional commanders and territorial governors for me: if you come today, the capital can still be saved; wait any longer and it will be too late!"

sentences.zh: 既而卒無至者。

translations.literal: Soon afterward in the end none arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In the end, not one came.

sentences.zh: 征南將軍山簡遣督護王萬將兵入援，軍於涅陽，為王如所敗。

translations.literal: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian dispatched Supervisor Wang Wan to lead troops to enter in relief; the army encamped at Niyang and was defeated by Wang Ru.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Conquers the South Shan Jian sent Supervisor Wang Wan with troops to relieve the capital; they encamped at Niyang and were defeated by Wang Ru.

sentences.zh: 如遂大掠沔、漢，進逼襄陽，簡嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Wang Ru thereupon plundered greatly in the Mian and Han regions, advanced to press Xiangyang, and Shan Jian held the city with a closed defense.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru then ravaged the Mian and Han valleys, pressed toward Xiangyang, and Shan Jian shut himself within the city walls.

sentences.zh: 荊州刺史王澄自將，欲援京師，至沶口，聞簡敗，眾散而還。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng, Inspector of Jing Province, personally led troops wishing to rescue the capital; when he reached Yikou and heard that Shan Jian had been defeated, his forces dispersed and he returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng, Inspector of Jing Province, personally led an army toward the capital, but when he reached Yikou and learned of Shan Jian's defeat, his men scattered and he turned back.

sentences.zh: 朝議多欲遷都以避難，王衍以為不可，賣車牛以安眾心。

translations.literal: Court deliberations mostly wished to move the capital to escape calamity; Wang Yan thought it could not be done and sold carts and oxen to settle the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Most at court favored moving the capital to escape disaster; Wang Yan argued against it and sold off carts and oxen to reassure the people.

sentences.zh: 山簡為嚴嶷所逼，自襄陽徙屯夏口。

translations.literal: Shan Jian, pressed by Yan Ni, moved from Xiangyang to encamp at Xiakou.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed by Yan Ni, Shan Jian withdrew from Xiangyang and encamped at Xiakou.

sentences.zh: 石勒引兵濟河，將趣南陽，王如、侯脫、嚴嶷等聞之，遣眾一萬屯襄城以拒勒。

translations.literal: Shi Le led troops across the river, intending to press toward Nanyang; Wang Ru, Hou Tuo, Yan Ni, and the others, hearing of this, dispatched ten thousand men to encamp at Xiangcheng to resist Shi Le.
