translations.idiomatic: Shi Le crossed the river heading for Nanyang; when Wang Ru, Hou Tuo, Yan Ni, and their allies heard of it, they sent ten thousand men to hold Xiangcheng against him.

sentences.zh: 勒擊之，盡俘其眾，進屯宛北。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked them, captured their entire force, and advanced to encamp north of Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked, took every man captive, and advanced to camp north of Wan.

sentences.zh: 是時，侯脫據宛，王如據穰。

translations.literal: At this time Hou Tuo held Wan, and Wang Ru held Rang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hou Tuo held Wan and Wang Ru held Rang.

sentences.zh: 如素與脫不協，遣使重賂勒，結為兄弟，說勒使攻脫。

translations.literal: Wang Ru had long been at odds with Hou Tuo; he dispatched envoys with heavy bribes to Shi Le, entered into brotherhood with him, and urged Shi Le to attack Hou Tuo.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ru had long been at odds with Hou Tuo; he sent envoys laden with gifts to Shi Le, swore brotherhood with him, and urged him to attack Hou Tuo.

sentences.zh: 勒攻宛，克之；

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Wan and captured it;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Wan and took it;

sentences.zh: 嚴嶷引兵救宛，不及而降。

translations.literal: Yan Ni led troops to rescue Wan, but did not arrive in time and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ni marched to relieve Wan, arrived too late, and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 勒斬脫；

translations.literal: Shi Le executed Hou Tuo;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le executed Hou Tuo;

sentences.zh: 囚嶷，送於平陽，盡並其眾。

translations.literal: he imprisoned Yan Ni and sent him to Pingyang, and fully absorbed his forces.
translations.idiomatic: he imprisoned Yan Ni and sent him to Pingyang, absorbing all his troops.

sentences.zh: 遂南寇襄陽，攻拔江西壘壁三十餘所。

translations.literal: He thereupon raided south toward Xiangyang and captured more than thirty fortified camps west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided south toward Xiangyang and captured more than thirty fortified camps west of the river.

sentences.zh: 還，趣襄城，王如遣弟璃襲勒；

translations.literal: On his return, as he pressed toward Xiangcheng, Wang Ru sent his younger brother Wang Li to attack Shi Le;
translations.idiomatic: On the return march toward Xiangcheng, Wang Ru sent his younger brother Wang Li to strike at Shi Le;

sentences.zh: 勒迎擊，滅之，復屯江西。

translations.literal: Shi Le went out to meet the attack, destroyed them, and again encamped west of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le met the attack head-on, wiped them out, and again encamped west of the river.

sentences.zh: 太傅越既殺王延等，大失眾望；

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue, having already killed Wang Yan and the others, greatly lost the people's esteem;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue had already put Wang Yan and others to death and lost much of the people's respect;

sentences.zh: 又以胡寇益盛，內不自安，乃戎服入見，請討石勒，且鎮集兗、豫。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the barbarian invaders grew ever stronger, he was inwardly ill at ease; he thereupon entered in military dress to have audience and requested to attack Shi Le and also to stabilize and gather Yan and Yu.
translations.idiomatic: With the barbarian invaders growing stronger, he felt increasingly insecure; he appeared at court in armor and asked permission to campaign against Shi Le and to stabilize Yan and Yu.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今胡虜侵逼郊畿，人無固志，朝廷社稷，倚賴於公，豈可遠出以孤根本！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Now the barbarian invaders press upon the capital suburbs; the people have no firm resolve; the court and altars rely upon you, Sir—how can you go far away and leave the root isolated!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The barbarians now press upon the capital's outskirts; the people have lost their resolve; the court and the realm depend on you—how can you go far away and leave the heart of the state undefended!"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣出，幸而破賊，則國威可振，猶愈於坐待困窮也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "When your servant goes out, if by good fortune we break the bandits, then national prestige can be revived—it is still better than sitting and awaiting exhaustion."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "If I take the field and by good fortune defeat the enemy, national prestige can be restored—that is still better than sitting here until we are worn down to nothing."

sentences.zh: 十一月，甲戌，越帥甲士四萬向許昌，留妃裴氏、世子毘及龍驤將軍李惲、右衛將軍何倫守衛京師，防察宮省；

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, Sima Yue led forty thousand armored troops toward Xuchang; he left his consort Lady Pei, his heir Sima Pi, General of the Dragon Cavalry Li Yun, and General of the Right Guard He Lun to guard the capital and keep watch over the palace and offices;
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on jiaxu, Sima Yue marched forty thousand armored troops toward Xuchang, leaving his consort Lady Pei, his heir Sima Pi, General of the Dragon Cavalry Li Yun, and General of the Right Guard He Lun to defend the capital and watch over the palace.

sentences.zh: 以潘滔為河南尹，總留事。

translations.literal: He appointed Pan Tao Administrator of Henan and put him in overall charge of affairs left behind.
translations.idiomatic: He made Pan Tao Administrator of Henan and put him in charge of all affairs at the capital.

sentences.zh: 越表以行台自隨，用太尉衍為軍司，朝賢素望，悉為佐吏，名將勁卒，咸入其府。

translations.literal: Sima Yue memorialized to have a mobile headquarters accompany him; he used Grand Commandant Wang Yan as army adviser; eminent ministers of long-standing repute all became his staff officers, and famous generals and crack troops all entered his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue memorialized to take a mobile headquarters with him, made Grand Commandant Wang Yan his army adviser, drew every eminent minister of standing into his staff, and gathered famous generals and crack troops into his command.

sentences.zh: 於是宮省無復守衛，荒饉日甚，殿內死人交橫；

translations.literal: Thereupon the palace and offices no longer had guards; famine grew daily worse, and corpses lay piled within the halls;
translations.idiomatic: The palace and offices were left without guards; famine worsened by the day, and corpses piled up inside the halls;

sentences.zh: 盜賊公行，府寺營署，並掘塹自守。

translations.literal: bandits walked openly in the streets, and government offices and barracks all dug moats to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: robbers roamed openly, and every government office and barracks dug moats to defend itself.

sentences.zh: 越東屯項，以馮嵩為左司馬，自領豫州牧。

translations.literal: Sima Yue encamped east at Xiang; he appointed Feng Song Left Major and personally assumed the governorship of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue encamped east at Xiang, made Feng Song his Left Major, and took personal charge as Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王楙白帝遣兵襲何倫，不克；

translations.literal: Sima Mao, Prince of Jingling, informed the emperor and dispatched troops to attack He Lun, but did not succeed;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mao, Prince of Jingling, persuaded the emperor to send troops against He Lun, but the attack failed;

sentences.zh: 帝委罪於楙，楙逃竄，得免。

translations.literal: the emperor laid the blame on Sima Mao; Sima Mao fled and escaped punishment.
translations.idiomatic: the emperor blamed Sima Mao, who fled and escaped punishment.

sentences.zh: 揚州都督周馥以洛陽孤危，上書請遷都壽春。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu, Supervisor of Yang Province, because Luoyang was isolated and imperiled, submitted a memorial requesting that the capital be moved to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu, Supervisor of Yang Province, finding Luoyang isolated and imperiled, memorialized the throne to move the capital to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 太傅越以馥不先白己而直上書，大怒，召馥及淮南太守裴碩。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Sima Yue, because Zhou Fu had not first informed him but submitted directly to the throne, was greatly enraged and summoned Zhou Fu and Pei Shuo, Administrator of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Sima Yue was furious that Zhou Fu had gone over his head to the throne and summoned Zhou Fu and Pei Shuo, Administrator of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 馥不肯行，令碩帥兵先進。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu was unwilling to go and ordered Pei Shuo to lead troops forward first.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu refused to go and ordered Pei Shuo to advance with troops first.

sentences.zh: 碩詐稱受越密旨，襲馥，為馥所敗，退保東城。

translations.literal: Pei Shuo falsely claimed to have received Sima Yue's secret order and attacked Zhou Fu; he was defeated by Zhou Fu and withdrew to hold Dongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuo falsely claimed a secret order from Sima Yue and attacked Zhou Fu, but Zhou Fu defeated him and drove him back to Dongcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔加張軌鎮西將軍、都督隴右諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict promoted Zhang Gui to General Who Guards the West and Supervisor of All Military Affairs in the lands west of Long.
translations.idiomatic: An edict promoted Zhang Gui to General Who Guards the West and gave him overall military command west of Long.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫傅祗、太常摯虞遣軌書，告以京師饑匱。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi and Minister of Ceremonies Zhi Yu sent Zhang Gui a letter informing him of hunger and destitution in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Fu Zhi and Minister of Ceremonies Zhi Yu wrote to Zhang Gui reporting famine and destitution in the capital.

sentences.zh: 軌遣參軍杜勳獻馬五百匹，毯布三萬匹。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui dispatched his aide Du Xun to present five hundred horses and thirty thousand bolts of felt and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui sent his aide Du Xun with five hundred horses and thirty thousand bolts of felt and cloth as tribute.

sentences.zh: 成太傅驤攻譙登於涪城。

translations.literal: Sima Xiang, Grand Tutor of Cheng, attacked Qiao Deng at Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiang, Grand Tutor of Cheng, besieged Qiao Deng at Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 羅尚子宇及參佐素惡登，不給其糧。

translations.literal: Luo Shang's son Luo Yu and his staff had long hated Qiao Deng and did not supply him with grain.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang's son Luo Yu and the staff had long resented Qiao Deng and refused to send him provisions.

sentences.zh: 益州刺史皮素怒，欲治其罪；

translations.literal: Pi Su, Inspector of Yi Province, was enraged and wished to punish them for their offense;
translations.idiomatic: Pi Su, Inspector of Yi Province, was furious and meant to punish them;

sentences.zh: 十二月，素至巴郡，羅宇等使人夜殺素，建平都尉暴重殺宇，巴郡亂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when Pi Su reached Ba commandery, Luo Yu and the others had men kill Pi Su by night; Bao Chong, Commandant of Jianping, killed Luo Yu, and Ba commandery fell into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when Pi Su reached Ba commandery, Luo Yu and his allies had him killed by night; Bao Chong, Commandant of Jianping, then killed Luo Yu, and Ba commandery descended into chaos.

sentences.zh: 驤知登食盡援絕，攻涪愈急。

translations.literal: Sima Xiang, knowing that Qiao Deng's food was exhausted and relief cut off, pressed the attack on Fu ever more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Qiao Deng's food was gone and no relief was coming, Sima Xiang pressed the siege of Fu ever harder.

sentences.zh: 士民皆熏鼠食之，餓死甚眾，無一人離叛者。

translations.literal: Officers and common people all smoked rats and ate them; very many died of starvation, yet not one deserted or rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers and civilians smoked rats for food; starvation killed many, yet not one deserted or turned traitor.

sentences.zh: 驤子壽先在登所，登乃歸之。

translations.literal: Sima Xiang's son Shou was earlier in Qiao Deng's custody; Qiao Deng thereupon returned him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiang's son Shou was being held by Qiao Deng, who now returned him unharmed.

sentences.zh: 三府官屬表巴東監軍南陽韓松為益州刺史，治巴東。

translations.literal: The officials of the Three Offices memorialized Han Song of Nanyang, Overseer of Military Affairs in Badong, as Inspector of Yi Province, with his seat of government in Badong.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the Three Offices memorialized Han Song of Nanyang, military overseer in Badong, as Inspector of Yi Province with his seat at Badong.

sentences.zh: 初，帝以王彌、石勒侵逼京畿，詔苟晞督帥州郡討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Wang Mi and Shi Le pressed upon the capital suburbs, the emperor issued an edict for Gou Xi to supervise and lead the provinces and commanderies in attacking them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with Wang Mi and Shi Le pressing upon the capital's outskirts, the emperor ordered Gou Xi to lead the provinces and commanderies against them.

sentences.zh: 會曹嶷破琅邪，北收齊地，兵勢甚盛，苟純閉城自守。

translations.literal: Just then Cao Ni broke Langye, gathered Qi territory in the north, and his military power was very strong; Gou Chun shut the city and held it in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Cao Ni overran Langye and swept north through Qi; his army grew formidable, and Gou Chun shut himself within the city walls.

sentences.zh: 晞還救青川，與嶷連戰，破之。

translations.literal: Gou Xi returned to rescue Qing Province, fought Cao Ni in succession, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi marched back to relieve Qing Province, fought Cao Ni in a series of battles, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，寧州刺史王遜到官，表李釗為朱提太守。

translations.literal: In this year, Wang Xun, Inspector of Ning Province, arrived at his post and memorialized Li Zhao as Administrator of Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: That year Wang Xun, Inspector of Ning Province, took office and memorialized Li Zhao as Administrator of Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 時寧州外逼於成，內有夷寇，城邑丘墟。

translations.literal: At that time Ning Province was pressed externally by Cheng and had barbarian raids within; cities and towns were heaps of ruins.
translations.idiomatic: Ning Province was menaced by Cheng from without and ravaged by tribal raids within; towns lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 遜惡衣菜食，招集離散，勞徠不倦，數年之間，州境復安。

translations.literal: Wang Xun wore coarse clothes and ate plain food, gathered the scattered, and toiled to win people back without tiring; within a few years the province's territory was restored to peace.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xun lived plainly, gathered the displaced, and worked tirelessly to win people back; within a few years the province was at peace again.

sentences.zh: 誅豪右不奉法者十餘家；

translations.literal: He executed more than ten powerful families who did not obey the law;
translations.idiomatic: He executed more than ten powerful families who defied the law;

sentences.zh: 以五苓夷昔為亂首，擊滅之，內外震服。

translations.literal: because the Wuling Yi had formerly been leaders of rebellion, he attacked and destroyed them, and within and without all were awed into submission.
translations.idiomatic: he crushed the Wuling Yi, who had once led rebellions, and awe settled over the province within and without.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰自以越次而立，忌其嫡兄恭；

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Cong, because he had ascended out of turn, was jealous of his legitimate elder brother Liu Gong;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong, ruler of Han, knowing he had taken the throne out of turn, feared his legitimate elder brother Liu Gong;

sentences.zh: 因恭寢，穴其壁間，刺而殺之。

translations.literal: while Liu Gong was asleep, he bored through the wall and stabbed and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: while Liu Gong slept, he bored through the wall and stabbed him to death.

sentences.zh: 漢太后單氏卒，漢主聰尊母張氏為皇太后。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Shan of Han died; the Han ruler Liu Cong honored his mother Lady Zhang as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Shan of Han died, and Liu Cong, ruler of Han, honored his own mother Lady Zhang as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 單氏年少美色，聰烝焉。

translations.literal: Lady Shan was young and beautiful; Liu Cong took her to his bed.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shan was young and beautiful, and Liu Cong took her as his consort.

sentences.zh: 太弟乂屢以為言，單氏慚恚而死。

translations.literal: The Imperial Younger Brother Liu Yi repeatedly spoke out against it; Lady Shan died of shame and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Younger Brother Liu Yi protested again and again; Lady Shan died of shame and grief.

sentences.zh: 乂寵由是漸衰，然以單氏故，尚未之廢也。

translations.literal: Liu Yi's favor thereby gradually waned, yet because of Lady Shan he had not yet been deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi's standing gradually declined, but because of Lady Shan he had not yet been removed from succession.

sentences.zh: 呼延後言於聰曰：「父死子繼，古今常道。

translations.literal: Empress Huyan said to Liu Cong: "When a father dies the son succeeds—this is the constant way from ancient times to the present.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Huyan said to Liu Cong: "When a father dies, the son succeeds—that is the way of the world, ancient and modern alike.

sentences.zh: 陛下承高祖之業，太弟何為者哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty inherits the enterprise of Emperor Gaozu—what purpose does the Imperial Younger Brother serve!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty inherits the legacy of Emperor Gaozu—what place is there for an Imperial Younger Brother!

sentences.zh: 陛下百年後，粲兄弟必無種矣。」

translations.literal: After Your Majesty's hundred years, Liu Can's brothers will surely be exterminated to the last seed."
translations.idiomatic: When Your Majesty is gone, Liu Can and his brothers will not survive."

sentences.zh: 聰曰：「然，吾當徐思之。」

translations.literal: Liu Cong said: "So it is; I shall consider the matter at leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong said: "True—but I shall think on it at my leisure."

sentences.zh: 呼延氏曰：「事留變生，太弟見粲兄弟浸長，必有不安之志，萬一有小人交構其間，未必不禍發於今日也。」

translations.literal: Lady Huyan said: "If matters are postponed, change will arise; when the Imperial Younger Brother sees Liu Can's brothers gradually growing, he will surely harbor unease; should petty men by chance weave intrigues between them, disaster might not wait until tomorrow to erupt."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huyan said: "Delay breeds trouble. When the Imperial Younger Brother sees Liu Can's brothers growing up, he will grow restless; if petty men should stir trouble between them, disaster may strike today, not tomorrow."

sentences.zh: 聰心然之。

translations.literal: Liu Cong was inwardly convinced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was persuaded.

sentences.zh: 乂舅光祿大夫單沖泣謂乂曰：「疏不間親。

translations.literal: Liu Yi's maternal uncle, Palace Attendant Shan Chong, weeping said to Liu Yi: "Outsiders cannot come between those who are kin.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi's maternal uncle, Palace Attendant Shan Chong, wept and said to him: "Outsiders cannot drive a wedge between kin.

sentences.zh: 主上有意於河內王矣，殿下何不避之！」

translations.literal: The emperor already favors the Prince of Henei—why does Your Highness not withdraw!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor already favors the Prince of Henei—why do you not step aside!"

sentences.zh: 乂曰：「河瑞之末，主上自惟嫡庶之分，以大位讓乂。

translations.literal: Liu Yi said: "At the end of the Herui era, the emperor himself weighed the distinction between legitimate and secondary sons and offered the great position to Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi said: "At the end of the Herui era, the emperor himself weighed the claims of legitimate and secondary sons and offered the throne to me.

sentences.zh: 乂以主上齒長，故相推奉。

translations.literal: Yi, because the emperor was older in years, therefore deferred and supported him.
translations.idiomatic: I yielded because he was my elder and supported him instead.

sentences.zh: 天下者，高祖之天下，兄終弟及，何為不可！

translations.literal: The realm belongs to Emperor Gaozu—when the elder brother dies, the younger succeeds; why should it not be so!
translations.idiomatic: The realm belongs to Emperor Gaozu—when an elder brother dies, a younger brother succeeds; why should that be forbidden!

sentences.zh: 粲兄弟既壯，猶今日也。

translations.literal: When Liu Can's brothers have grown strong, it will still be as it is today.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Can's brothers come of age, things will be as they are today.

sentences.zh: 且子弟之間，親疏詎幾，主上寧可有此意乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, among sons and younger brothers, how much difference is there between close and distant? Could the emperor truly harbor such intent!
translations.idiomatic: And among sons and younger brothers, what real difference is there between near and far? Could the emperor truly mean such a thing!

sentences.zh: 孝懷皇帝中永嘉五年（

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part, Yongjia Year Five (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huai of Jin, Middle Part—Yongjia, Year Five (

sentences.zh: 辛未，公元三一一年）

translations.literal: xinwei, CE 311)
translations.idiomatic: xinwei, 311 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，壬申，苟晞為曹嶷所敗，棄城奔高平。

translations.literal: In spring, in the first month, on renshen, Gou Xi was defeated by Cao Ni, abandoned his city, and fled to Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, in the first month, on renshen, Cao Ni defeated Gou Xi; Gou Xi abandoned his city and fled to Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 石勒謀保據江、漢，參軍都尉張賓以為不可。

translations.literal: Shi Le planned to hold and occupy the Yangtze and Han regions; Adjunct General Zhang Bin held that it was not feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le planned to hold the Yangtze-Han basin, but Adjunct General Zhang Bin argued against it.

sentences.zh: 會軍中饑疫，死者太半，乃渡沔，寇江夏，癸酉，拔之。

translations.literal: Just then famine and pestilence struck the army, and more than half the men died; he then crossed the Han River, raided Jiangxia, and on guiyou captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Famine and pestilence meanwhile ravaged his army, killing more than half his men; he then crossed the Han River, attacked Jiangxia, and on guiyou took the city.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，成太傅驤拔涪城，獲譙登。

translations.literal: On yihai, Cheng Grand Tutor Li Xiang captured Fucheng and took Qiao Deng prisoner.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai, Li Xiang, Grand Tutor of Cheng, captured Fucheng and took Qiao Deng prisoner.

sentences.zh: 太保始拔巴西，殺文石。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Shi captured Baxi and killed Wenshi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Shi captured Baxi and executed Wenshi.

sentences.zh: 於是成主雄大赦，改元玉衡。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Cheng ruler Li Xiong proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Yuheng.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Li Xiong, ruler of Cheng, declared a general amnesty and adopted the era name Yuheng.

sentences.zh: 譙登至成都，雄欲宥之；

translations.literal: When Qiao Deng arrived at Chengdu, Li Xiong wished to spare him;
translations.idiomatic: When Qiao Deng was brought to Chengdu, Li Xiong intended to show him mercy;

sentences.zh: 登詞氣不屈，雄殺之。

translations.literal: Qiao Deng's words and bearing were unyielding; Li Xiong had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao Deng spoke and carried himself without yielding; Li Xiong had him put to death.

sentences.zh: 巴蜀流民布在荊、湘間，數為土民所侵苦，蜀人李驤聚眾據樂鄉反，南平太守應詹與醴陵令杜苾共擊破之。

translations.literal: Refugees from Ba and Shu were scattered throughout the Jing and Xiang regions and were repeatedly harassed and oppressed by the local people; the Shu native Li Xiang gathered a crowd, seized Leyang, and rebelled; the Administrator of Nanping, Ying Zhan, together with the Magistrate of Liling, Du Mi, jointly attacked and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Refugees from Ba and Shu were scattered across Jing and Xiang and suffered repeated abuse at the hands of the locals; Li Xiang, a man of Shu, raised a force, seized Leyang, and rebelled—until Ying Zhan, Administrator of Nanping, and Du Mi, Magistrate of Liling, joined forces and routed him.

sentences.zh: 王澄使成都內史王機討驤，驤請降，澄偽許而襲殺之。

translations.literal: Wang Cheng sent Wang Ji, Interior Secretary of Chengdu, to attack Li Xiang; Li Xiang requested surrender, and Wang Cheng feigned acceptance then launched a surprise attack and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Cheng sent Wang Ji, Interior Secretary of Chengdu, against Li Xiang; Li Xiang offered to surrender, but Wang Cheng pretended to accept and then struck him down in a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 以其妻子為賞，沉八千餘人於江，流民益怨忿。

translations.literal: He offered their wives and children as rewards, drowned more than eight thousand people in the river, and the refugees grew ever more resentful.
translations.idiomatic: He offered their families as prizes to his troops, drowned more than eight thousand people in the river, and the refugees' hatred only deepened.

sentences.zh: 蜀人杜疇等復反，湘州參軍馮素與蜀人汝班有隙，言於刺史荀眺曰：「巴、蜀流民皆欲反。」

translations.literal: The Shu men Du Chou and others rebelled again; the Adjunct to the Inspector of Xiang Province, Feng Su, had a grudge against the Shu man Ru Ban, and said to the Inspector Xun Tiao: "The refugees from Ba and Shu all wish to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Du Chou of Shu and others rose again; Feng Su, an aide in the Xiangzhou headquarters, bore a grudge against Ru Ban, a fellow Shu exile, and told Inspector Xun Tiao: "Every refugee from Ba and Shu means to rebel."

sentences.zh: 眺信之，欲盡誅流民。

translations.literal: Xun Tiao believed him and wished to execute all the refugees.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Tiao believed him and planned to kill every refugee.

sentences.zh: 流民大懼，四五萬家一時俱反，以杜苾州裡重望，共推為主。

translations.literal: The refugees were greatly alarmed; forty or fifty thousand households rebelled all at once and, because Du Mi enjoyed great prestige within the province, jointly raised him as their leader.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, forty or fifty thousand refugee households rose at once; because Du Mi was highly esteemed in the province, they made him their leader.

sentences.zh: 苾自稱梁、益二州牧、領湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Du Mi styled himself Governor of the Two Provinces of Liang and Yi and Acting Inspector of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mi proclaimed himself Governor of Liang and Yi and Acting Inspector of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 裴碩求救於琅邪王睿，睿使揚威將軍甘卓等攻周馥於壽春。

translations.literal: Pei Shuo requested relief from Sima Rui, Prince of Langye; Rui sent General Who Displays Might Gan Zhuo and others to attack Zhou Fu at Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Shuo appealed to Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, who sent Gan Zhuo, General Who Displays Might, and others to attack Zhou Fu at Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 馥眾潰，奔項，豫州都督新蔡王確執之，馥憂憤而卒。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu's forces collapsed; he fled to Xiang; Sima Que, Prince of Xincai, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in Yu Province, seized him, and Zhou Fu died in grief and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu's army broke and fled to Xiang; Sima Que, Prince of Xincai and supervisor of Yu Province, took him prisoner, and Zhou Fu died of grief and rage.

sentences.zh: 確，騰之子也。

translations.literal: Sima Que was the son of Sima Teng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Que was a son of Sima Teng.

sentences.zh: 揚州刺史劉陶卒。

translations.literal: Liu Tao, Inspector of Yang Province, died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tao, Inspector of Yang Province, died.

sentences.zh: 琅邪王睿復以安東軍咨祭酒王敦為揚州刺史，尋加都督征討諸軍事。

translations.literal: Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, again appointed Wang Dun, Adviser-Director of Sacrifices to the Army of Pacification of the East, as Inspector of Yang Province, and shortly afterward added the title Supervisor of All Military Affairs for Campaigning and Suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Rui again made Wang Dun, chief staff officer of the Army of Pacification of the East, Inspector of Yang Province, and soon afterward made him supervisor of all military affairs for campaigning and suppression.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，平原王干薨。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Sima Gan, Prince of Pingyuan, died.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen, Sima Gan, Prince of Pingyuan, died.

sentences.zh: 二月，石勒攻新蔡，殺新蔡莊王確於南頓；

translations.literal: In the second month, Shi Le attacked Xincai and killed Sima Que, Prince Zhuang of Xincai, at Nandun;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, Shi Le attacked Xincai and killed Sima Que, Prince Zhuang of Xincai, at Nandun;

sentences.zh: 進拔許昌，殺平東將軍王康。

translations.literal: advancing to capture Xuchang and kill General Who Pacifies the East Wang Kang.
translations.idiomatic: then marched on to take Xuchang and kill Wang Kang, General Who Pacifies the East.

sentences.zh: 氐苻成、隗文復叛，自宜都趣巴東；

translations.literal: The Di leaders Fu Cheng and Wei Wen rebelled again, going from Yidu toward Badong;
translations.idiomatic: Fu Cheng and Wei Wen of the Di rebelled again, marching from Yidu toward Badong;

sentences.zh: 建平都尉暴重討之。

translations.literal: Bao Chong, Commandant of Jianping, attacked them.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chong, Commandant of Jianping, moved against them.

sentences.zh: 重因殺韓松，自領三府事。

translations.literal: Bao Chong thereupon killed Han Song and took charge of the affairs of the Three Offices himself.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Chong then killed Han Song and assumed the duties of the Three Offices himself.

sentences.zh: 東海孝獻王越既與苟晞有隙，河南尹潘滔、尚書劉望等復從而譖之。

translations.literal: Sima Yue, Prince Xiaoxian of Donghai, having already been at odds with Gou Xi, Pan Tao, Intendant of Henan, Liu Wang, Master of Writing, and others again joined in slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue, Prince Xiaoxian of Donghai, was already at odds with Gou Xi when Pan Tao, Intendant of Henan, Liu Wang of the Masters of Writing, and others slandered Gou Xi as well.

sentences.zh: 晞怒，表求滔等首，揚言：「司馬元超為宰相不平，使天下淆亂，苟道將豈可以不義使之！」

translations.literal: Gou Xi was enraged; he memorialized requesting the heads of Pan Tao and the others, and declared publicly: "Sima Yuanchao is an unjust chancellor, throwing the realm into disorder—how can General Gou Daojiang be made to serve him in an unrighteous cause!"
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Gou Xi memorialized demanding the heads of Pan Tao and his allies and declared publicly: "Sima Yuanchao holds power unjustly and has thrown the realm into chaos—how can General Gou be made to serve such an unrighteous master!"

sentences.zh: 乃移檄諸州，自稱功伐，陳越罪狀。

translations.literal: He then issued a proclamation to the provinces, praising his own achievements and setting forth Sima Yue's crimes.
translations.idiomatic: He then circulated a proclamation to the provinces, boasting of his own merits and listing Sima Yue's crimes.

sentences.zh: 帝亦惡越專權，多違詔命；

translations.literal: The emperor also detested Sima Yue's monopoly of power and his frequent disregard of edicts;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor too hated Sima Yue's monopoly of power and his repeated defiance of imperial orders;

sentences.zh: 所留將士何倫等，抄掠公卿，逼辱公主；

translations.literal: the soldiers Sima Yue had left behind, including He Lun, plundered the nobles and officials and humiliated the princesses;
translations.idiomatic: the troops he had left behind, led by He Lun, pillaged the nobility and humiliated the imperial princesses;

sentences.zh: 密賜晞手詔，使討之。

translations.literal: he secretly bestowed upon Gou Xi an imperial letter in the emperor's own hand, ordering him to attack Sima Yue.
translations.idiomatic: and secretly sent Gou Xi an edict in the emperor's own hand ordering him to attack Sima Yue.

sentences.zh: 晞數與帝文書往來，越疑之，使游騎於成皋間伺之，果獲晞使及詔書。

translations.literal: Gou Xi and the emperor exchanged letters repeatedly; Sima Yue grew suspicious and sent roaming horsemen to watch between Chenggao; they indeed captured Gou Xi's messenger and the imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: Letters passed repeatedly between Gou Xi and the emperor; Sima Yue grew suspicious and posted mounted scouts around Chenggao—they captured Gou Xi's messenger and the secret edict.

sentences.zh: 乃下檄罪狀晞，以從事中郎楊瑁為兗州刺史，使與徐州刺史裴盾共討晞。

translations.literal: Sima Yue then issued a proclamation listing Gou Xi's crimes, appointed Yang Mao, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, as Inspector of Yan Province, and sent him with Pei Dun, Inspector of Xu Province, jointly to attack Gou Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue then published a proclamation accusing Gou Xi, made Yang Mao, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Inspector of Yan Province, and ordered him and Pei Dun, Inspector of Xu Province, to attack Gou Xi together.

sentences.zh: 晞遣騎收潘滔，滔夜遁，得免；

translations.literal: Gou Xi sent horsemen to seize Pan Tao; Pan Tao fled by night and escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi sent cavalry to seize Pan Tao, who fled by night and escaped;

sentences.zh: 執尚書劉曾、侍中程延，斬之。

translations.literal: he seized Liu Zeng, Master of Writing, and Cheng Yan, Palace Attendant, and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: he seized Liu Zeng of the Masters of Writing and Cheng Yan, Palace Attendant, and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 越憂憤成疾，以後事付王衍；

translations.literal: Sima Yue, grief and indignation turning to illness, entrusted his final affairs to Wang Yan;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yue fell ill with grief and rage and entrusted his final affairs to Wang Yan;

sentences.zh: 三月，丙子，薨於項，秘不發喪。

translations.literal: In the third month, on bingzi, he died at Xiang, and his death was kept secret without announcement of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on bingzi, he died at Xiang, and his death was kept secret.

sentences.zh: 眾共推衍為元帥，衍不敢當；

translations.literal: The troops jointly raised Wang Yan as commander-in-chief; Wang Yan did not dare accept;
translations.idiomatic: The army wanted Wang Yan as commander-in-chief, but he refused;

sentences.zh: 以讓襄陽王范，范亦不受。

translations.literal: he yielded the post to Sima Fan, Prince of Xiangyang, who also would not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: he offered command to Sima Fan, Prince of Xiangyang, who also declined.

sentences.zh: 范，瑋之子也。

translations.literal: Sima Fan was the son of Sima Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Fan was a son of Sima Wei.

sentences.zh: 於是衍等相與奉越喪還葬東海。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Yan and the others together escorted Sima Yue's coffin back to Donghai for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan and the others then escorted Sima Yue's coffin home to Donghai for burial.

sentences.zh: 何倫、李惲等聞越薨，奉裴妃及世子毘自洛陽東走，城中士民爭隨之。

translations.literal: When He Lun, Li Yun, and the others heard that Sima Yue had died, they escorted Lady Pei and the heir Pi eastward from Luoyang, and the officials and commoners in the city scrambled to follow them.
translations.idiomatic: When He Lun, Li Yun, and the others learned of Sima Yue's death, they escorted Lady Pei and the heir Pi east from Luoyang, and officials and commoners in the city thronged after them.

sentences.zh: 帝追貶越為縣王，以苟晞為大將軍、大都督，督青、徐、兗、豫、荊、揚六州諸軍事。

translations.literal: The emperor posthumously degraded Sima Yue to Prince of a Commandery and appointed Gou Xi as Grand General, Grand Commander, and Supervisor of All Military Affairs in the six provinces of Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor posthumously reduced Sima Yue to a commandery prince and made Gou Xi Grand General and Grand Commander, with authority over military affairs in Qing, Xu, Yan, Yu, Jing, and Yang.

sentences.zh: 益州將吏共殺暴重，表巴郡太守張羅行三府事。

translations.literal: The generals and officials of Yi Province jointly killed Bao Chong and memorialized Zhang Luo, Administrator of Ba Commandery, to conduct the affairs of the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Province's officers joined in killing Bao Chong and memorialized Zhang Luo, Administrator of Ba Commandery, to handle the affairs of the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 羅與隗文等戰，死，文等驅掠吏民，西降於成。

translations.literal: Zhang Luo fought Wei Wen and the others, was killed; Wei Wen and the others drove off and plundered officials and commoners and surrendered westward to Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Luo fought Wei Wen and the others and fell; they then drove and looted officials and commoners and surrendered westward to Cheng.

sentences.zh: 三府文武共表平西司馬蜀郡王異行三府事，領巴郡太守。

translations.literal: The civil and military officers of the Three Offices jointly memorialized Sima Yi, Prince of Shujun and Director of the Army of Pacification of the West, to conduct the affairs of the Three Offices and serve concurrently as Administrator of Ba Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officers of the Three Offices jointly memorialized Sima Yi, Prince of Shujun and director of the Army of Pacification of the West, to govern the Three Offices and serve concurrently as Administrator of Ba Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初，梁州刺史張光會諸郡守於魏興，共謀進取。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhang Guang, Inspector of Liang Province, gathered the administrators of the commanderies at Weixing to plan an advance.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Zhang Guang, Inspector of Liang Province, summoned the commandery administrators to Weixing to plan a campaign of reconquest.

sentences.zh: 張燕唱言：「漢中荒敗，迫近大賊，克復之事，當俟英雄。」

translations.literal: Zhang Yan declared publicly: "Hanzhong is desolate and ruined, pressed close upon by great rebels; the work of recovery must await a hero."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan declared publicly: "Hanzhong lies in ruins, right beside the enemy—reconquest must wait for a hero."

sentences.zh: 光以燕受鄧定略，致失漢中，今復沮眾，呵出斬之。

translations.literal: Zhang Guang, because Zhang Yan had accepted Deng Ding's surrender and thereby lost Hanzhong, and now again demoralized the troops, shouted him out and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guang held that Zhang Yan had accepted Deng Ding's surrender and thereby lost Hanzhong, and was now again discouraging the men—he had him dragged out and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 治兵進戰，累年乃得至漢中，綏撫荒殘，百姓悅服。

translations.literal: He drilled the troops and advanced to fight; only after several years did he reach Hanzhong, where he soothed and settled the desolate and ruined land, and the people were pleased and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his army and fought forward; only after several years did he reach Hanzhong, where he pacified the devastated countryside and won the people's willing submission.

sentences.zh: 夏，四月，石勒帥輕騎追太傅越之喪，及於苦縣寧平城，大敗晉兵，縱騎圍而射之，將士十餘萬人相踐如山，無一人得免者。

translations.literal: In summer, in the fourth month, Shi Le led light cavalry in pursuit of Grand Tutor Sima Yue's funeral procession, caught up with it at Ningping Fort in Ku County, routed the Jin forces, let his horsemen surround them and shoot; more than a hundred thousand officers and soldiers trampled one another like a mountain, and not one escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In summer, in the fourth month, Shi Le led light cavalry in pursuit of Grand Tutor Sima Yue's funeral train, caught it at Ningping Fort in Ku County, and routed the Jin army; he let his riders surround them and shoot until more than a hundred thousand officers and soldiers lay heaped in mountains of bodies—not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 執太尉衍、襄陽王范、任城王濟、武陵莊王澹、西河王喜、梁懷王禧、齊王超、吏部尚書劉望、廷尉諸葛銓、豫州刺史劉喬、太傅長史庚金全等，坐之幕下，問以晉故。

translations.literal: He seized Grand Commandant Wang Yan, Sima Fan Prince of Xiangyang, Sima Ji Prince of Rencheng, Sima Dan Prince Zhuang of Wuling, Sima Xi Prince of Xihe, Sima Xi Prince Huai of Liang, Sima Chao Prince of Qi, Liu Wang Director of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhuge Quan Director of Justice, Liu Qiao Inspector of Yu Province, Geng Jinquan Chief Clerk to the Grand Tutor, and others; seated them beneath his tent, he questioned them about Jin affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Grand Commandant Wang Yan, Sima Fan Prince of Xiangyang, Sima Ji Prince of Rencheng, Sima Dan Prince Zhuang of Wuling, Sima Xi Prince of Xihe, Sima Xi Prince Huai of Liang, Sima Chao Prince of Qi, Liu Wang of the Ministry of Personnel, Zhuge Quan the Chief of Justice, Liu Qiao Inspector of Yu Province, Geng Jinquan chief clerk to the Grand Tutor, and others; seated beneath his tent, he questioned them about affairs in Jin.

sentences.zh: 衍具陳禍敗之由，雲計不在己；

translations.literal: Wang Yan fully set forth the causes of disaster and defeat, saying the planning had not been his;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yan recounted at length the causes of Jin's collapse, insisting that the planning had not been his;

sentences.zh: 且自言少無宦情，不豫世事；

translations.literal: moreover he declared that from youth he had had no taste for office and had not involved himself in worldly affairs;
translations.idiomatic: and claimed that from youth he had no taste for office and had kept clear of worldly affairs;

sentences.zh: 因勸勒稱尊號，冀以自免。

translations.literal: thereupon he urged Shi Le to assume an exalted title, hoping thereby to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: he then urged Shi Le to take an imperial title, hoping to save his own skin.

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「君少壯登朝，名蓋四海，身居重任，何得言無宦情邪！

translations.literal: Shi Le said: "You entered court while still young and strong, your fame covering the four seas, holding a weighty post—how can you say you had no taste for office!
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said: "You entered court young, your fame filled the realm, you held weighty office—how can you say you never wanted power!

sentences.zh: 破壞天下，非君而誰！」

translations.literal: Who but you ruined the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: Who else ruined the realm but you!"

sentences.zh: 命左右扶出。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to help Wang Yan out.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his attendants to lead him away.

sentences.zh: 眾人畏死，多自陳述。

translations.literal: The others, fearing death, mostly spoke up for themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The others, fearing death, mostly pleaded their own cases.

sentences.zh: 獨襄陽王范神色儼然，顧呵之曰：「今日之事，何復紛紜！」

translations.literal: Only Sima Fan, Prince of Xiangyang, bore himself with stern composure; turning, he shouted at them: "Today's affair—why this further clamor!"
translations.idiomatic: Only Sima Fan, Prince of Xiangyang, remained stern and unmoved; turning on the others he shouted: "Today is the day—why this wrangling!"

sentences.zh: 勒謂孔萇曰：「吾行天下多矣，未嘗見此輩人，當可存乎？」

translations.literal: Shi Le said to Kong Chang: "I have traveled the realm widely and never seen men like these—might they be spared?"
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said to Kong Chang: "I have ranged across the realm and never seen men like these—could they be spared?"

sentences.zh: 萇曰：「彼皆晉之王公，終不為吾用。」

translations.literal: Kong Chang said: "They are all great lords and nobles of Jin; in the end they will not serve us."
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chang said: "They are Jin's royal princes and grandees—they will never serve us in the end."

sentences.zh: 勒曰：「雖然，要不可加以鋒刃。」

translations.literal: Shi Le said: "Even so, one must not put the blade to them."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said: "Even so, they must not be put to the sword."

sentences.zh: 夜，使人排牆殺之。

translations.literal: By night he had men knock down a wall and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: By night he had men knock down a wall and crush them to death.

sentences.zh: 濟，宣帝弟子景王陵之子；

translations.literal: Sima Ji was the son of Sima Ling, Prince Jing of Rencheng;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ji was a son of Sima Ling, Prince Jing of Rencheng;

sentences.zh: 禧，澹之子也。

translations.literal: Sima Xi was the son of Sima Dan.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xi, Prince Huai of Liang, was a son of Sima Dan, Prince Zhuang of Wuling.

sentences.zh: 剖越柩，焚其屍，曰：「亂天下者此人也，吾為天下報之，故焚其骨以告天地。」

translations.literal: Shi Le cut open Sima Yue's coffin and burned his corpse, saying: "This is the man who threw the realm into disorder; I am avenging the realm, therefore I burn his bones to announce it to Heaven and Earth."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le opened Sima Yue's coffin and burned the body, declaring: "This man threw the realm into chaos; I avenge the realm, and burn his bones to announce it to Heaven and Earth."

sentences.zh: 何倫等至洧倉，遇勒，戰敗，東海世子毘及宗室四十八王皆沒於勒，何倫奔下邳，李惲奔廣宗。

translations.literal: When He Lun and the others reached Weicang, they encountered Shi Le, were defeated; Sima Pi, heir of Donghai, and forty-eight princes of the imperial clan all fell into Shi Le's hands; He Lun fled to Xiapi, Li Yun fled to Guangzong.
translations.idiomatic: He Lun and his party reached Weicang, met Shi Le, and were routed; Sima Pi, heir to the Donghai house, and forty-eight princes of the imperial clan all fell into Shi Le's hands; He Lun fled to Xiapi and Li Yun to Guangzong.

sentences.zh: 裴妃為人所掠賣，久之，渡江。

translations.literal: Lady Pei was seized and sold by others; after a long time she crossed the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Pei was captured and sold into bondage; long afterward she crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 初，琅邪王睿之鎮建業，裴妃意也，故睿德之，厚加存撫，以其子沖繼越後。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, had been stationed at Jianye, it had been at Lady Pei's urging; therefore Rui felt indebted to her and treated her with particular generosity, having his son Chong succeed to Sima Yue's line.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Lady Pei had urged Sima Rui to take up his post at Jianye; Rui therefore felt deep gratitude toward her, treated her with great generosity, and had his son Chong succeed to Sima Yue's lineage.

sentences.zh: 漢趙固、王桑攻裴盾，殺之。

translations.literal: Guo Gu and Wang Sang of Han attacked Pei Dun and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Gu and Wang Sang of Han attacked Pei Dun and killed him.

sentences.zh: 杜苾攻長沙。

translations.literal: Du Mi attacked Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mi attacked Changsha.

sentences.zh: 五月，荀眺棄城奔廣州，苾追擒之。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Xun Tiao abandoned his city and fled to Guangzhou; Du Mi pursued and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, Xun Tiao abandoned his city and fled to Guangzhou; Du Mi pursued and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 於是苾南破零、桂，東掠武昌，殺二千石長吏甚眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon Du Mi broke Ling and Gui in the south, plundered eastward as far as Wuchang, and killed a great many officials of the two-thousand-dan rank and local administrators.
translations.idiomatic: Du Mi then overran Ling and Gui in the south, raided east as far as Wuchang, and killed a great many senior officials and local magistrates.

sentences.zh: 以太子太傅傅祗為司徒，尚書令荀籓為司空，加王浚大司馬、侍中、大都督，督幽、冀諸軍事，南陽王模為太尉、大都督，張軌為車騎大將軍，琅邪王睿為鎮東大將軍，兼督揚、江、湘、交、廣五州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Fu Zhi, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, was made Minister over the Masses; Xun Fan, Director of the Masters of Writing, was made Minister of Works; Wang Jun was promoted to Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, and Grand Commander, Supervisor of All Military Affairs in You and Ji provinces; Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, was made Grand Commandant and Grand Commander; Zhang Gui was made General of Chariots and Cavalry; Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, was made General Who Pacifies the East and concurrently Supervisor of All Military Affairs in the five provinces of Yang, Jiang, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Zhi, Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince, was appointed Minister over the Masses; Xun Fan, Director of the Masters of Writing, became Minister of Works; Wang Jun was promoted to Grand Marshal, Palace Attendant, and Grand Commander over You and Ji; Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, became Grand Commandant and Grand Commander; Zhang Gui became General of Chariots and Cavalry; and Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, became General Who Pacifies the East with concurrent authority over military affairs in Yang, Jiang, Xiang, Jiao, and Guang.

sentences.zh: 初，太傅越以南陽王模不能綏撫關中，表徵為司空。

translations.literal: Earlier, Grand Tutor Sima Yue, because Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, could not pacify and settle Guanzhong, memorialized that he be recalled to serve as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Grand Tutor Sima Yue, finding that Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, could not pacify Guanzhong, memorialized to recall him as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 將軍淳于定說模使不就徵，模從之；

translations.literal: General Chunyu Ding urged Sima Mo not to obey the recall, and Sima Mo followed his advice;
translations.idiomatic: General Chunyu Ding urged Sima Mo to refuse the recall, and he agreed;

sentences.zh: 表遣世子保為平西中郎將，鎮上邽，秦州刺史裴苞拒之。

translations.literal: he memorialized to send his heir Sima Bao as General of the Gentlemen of the Household for Pacification of the West to garrison Shanggui; Pei Bao, Inspector of Qin Province, barred him.
translations.idiomatic: he memorialized to send his heir Sima Bao as General of the Gentlemen of the Household for Pacification of the West to garrison Shanggui, but Pei Bao, Inspector of Qin Province, blocked him.

sentences.zh: 模使帳下都尉陳安攻苞，苞奔安定，太守賈疋納之。

translations.literal: Sima Mo sent Chen An, Commandant under his banner, to attack Pei Bao; Pei Bao fled to Anding, and the Administrator Jia Pi received him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo sent Chen An, a commandant under his banner, against Pei Bao; Pei Bao fled to Anding, where Administrator Jia Pi took him in.

sentences.zh: 苟晞表請遷都倉垣，使從事中郎劉會將船數十艘、宿衛五百人、穀千斛迎帝。

translations.literal: Gou Xi memorialized requesting that the capital be moved to Cangyuan and sent Liu Hui, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, with several dozen boats, five hundred palace guards, and a thousand hu of grain to welcome the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi memorialized to move the capital to Cangyuan and sent Liu Hui, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, with several dozen boats, five hundred palace guards, and a thousand hu of grain to escort the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝將從之，公卿猶豫，左右戀資財，遂不果行。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to agree, but the nobles and officials hesitated and those around him clung to their possessions; the move therefore did not take place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was ready to agree, but court officials hesitated and his attendants refused to abandon their possessions, so the move never happened.

sentences.zh: 既而洛陽饑困，人相食，百官流亡者什八九。

translations.literal: Before long Luoyang suffered famine and distress; men ate one another, and eight or nine tenths of the officials fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Luoyang was starving; people ate one another, and eight or nine tenths of the officials fled.

sentences.zh: 帝召公卿議，將行而衛從不備。

translations.literal: The emperor summoned the nobles and officials for consultation; he was about to depart but his guard and retinue were inadequate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned court officials to discuss flight, but his guard and escort were too thin.

sentences.zh: 帝撫手歎曰：「如何曾無車輿！」

translations.literal: The emperor clapped his hands and sighed, saying: "How is it that there is not even a carriage!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrung his hands and sighed: "How can there be not a single carriage!"

sentences.zh: 乃使傅祗出詣河陰，治舟楫，朝士數十人導從。

translations.literal: He then sent Fu Zhi out to Heyin to ready boats and oars, with several dozen court officials to guide and attend him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fu Zhi to Heyin to prepare boats, attended by several dozen court officials.

sentences.zh: 帝步出西掖門，至銅駝街，為盜所掠，不得進而還。

translations.literal: The emperor walked out through the Western Side Gate, reached Bronze Camel Street, was plundered by robbers, and unable to proceed returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor walked out through the Western Side Gate as far as Bronze Camel Street, was robbed by bandits, and had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 度支校尉東郡魏浚，帥流民數百家保河陰之硤石，時劫掠得穀麥，獻之。

translations.literal: Wei Jun of Dong Commandery, Revenue Controller, led several hundred refugee households in holding Xiashi at Heyin; at the time he had plundered grain and wheat and presented it as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun of Dong Commandery, Revenue Controller, held Xiashi at Heyin with several hundred refugee households; he had recently looted grain and wheat and now presented it to the court.

sentences.zh: 帝以為揚威將軍、平陽太守，度支如故。

translations.literal: The emperor appointed him General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Pingyang, his revenue duties continuing as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor made him General Who Displays Might and Administrator of Pingyang while keeping him in his revenue post.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰使前軍大將軍呼延晏將兵二萬七千寇洛陽，比及河南，晉兵前後十二敗，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: The Han ruler Liu Cong sent Front Army Grand General Huyan Yan with twenty-seven thousand troops to raid Luoyang; by the time he reached Henan, Jin forces had been defeated twelve times in succession, and more than thirty thousand men had died.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong sent Huyan Yan, Grand General of the Front Army, with twenty-seven thousand men against Luoyang; by the time he reached Henan, Jin armies had suffered twelve defeats in succession and more than thirty thousand men lay dead.

sentences.zh: 始安王曜、王彌、石勒皆引兵會之；

translations.literal: Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, Wang Mi, and Shi Le all led troops to join him;
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, Wang Mi, and Shi Le all marched to join him;

sentences.zh: 未至，晏留輜重於張方故壘；

translations.literal: before they arrived, Huyan Yan left the baggage train at the old fort of Zhang Fang;
translations.idiomatic: before they arrived, Huyan Yan left his baggage train at Zhang Fang's old fort;

sentences.zh: 癸未，先至洛陽；

translations.literal: on guiwei he reached Luoyang first;
translations.idiomatic: on guiwei he reached Luoyang ahead of them;

sentences.zh: 甲申，攻平昌門；

translations.literal: on jiashen he attacked the Pingchang Gate;
translations.idiomatic: on jiashen he assaulted the Pingchang Gate;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，克之，遂焚東陽門及諸府寺。

translations.literal: on bingxu he captured it, then burned the Dongyang Gate and the various government offices and temples.
translations.idiomatic: on bingxu he breached it, then burned the Dongyang Gate and the government offices.

sentences.zh: 六月，丁亥朔，晏以外繼不至，俘掠而去。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on the first day dinghai, because the reinforcements from outside had not arrived, Huyan Yan carried off captives and plunder and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on the new moon of dinghai, Huyan Yan withdrew after looting the city, since the outer reinforcements had not arrived.

sentences.zh: 帝具舟於洛水，將東走，晏盡焚之。

translations.literal: The emperor had prepared boats on the Luo River, planning to flee eastward; Huyan Yan burned them all.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had boats readied on the Luo River for a flight eastward; Huyan Yan burned them all.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，荀籓及弟光祿大夫組奔轘轅。

translations.literal: On gengyin, Xun Fan and his younger brother Zu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, fled to Huanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, Xun Fan and his younger brother Zu, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, fled to Huanyuan Pass.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，王彌至宣陽門；

translations.literal: On xinmao, Wang Mi reached the Xuanyang Gate;
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, Wang Mi reached the Xuanyang Gate;

sentences.zh: 壬辰，始安王曜至西明門；

translations.literal: On renchen, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, reached the Ximing Gate;
translations.idiomatic: On renchen, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, reached the Ximing Gate;

sentences.zh: 丁酉，王彌、呼延晏克宣陽門，入南宮，升太極前殿，縱兵大掠，悉收宮人、珍寶。

translations.literal: On dingyou, Wang Mi and Huyan Yan captured the Xuanyang Gate, entered the Southern Palace, ascended the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate, let the troops plunder on a great scale, and seized all the palace women and precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Wang Mi and Huyan Yan breached the Xuanyang Gate, entered the Southern Palace, and mounted the front hall of the Hall of Supreme Ultimate; they unleashed their troops in a great sack of the city and seized every palace woman and treasure they could find.

sentences.zh: 帝出華林園門，欲奔長安，漢兵追執之，幽於端門。

translations.literal: The emperor went out through the Huaglin Garden Gate, intending to flee to Chang'an; Han troops pursued and seized him and confined him at the Duan Gate.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor slipped out through the Huaglin Garden Gate, intending to flee to Chang'an; Han soldiers pursued, seized him, and held him captive at the Duan Gate.

sentences.zh: 曜自西明門入屯武庫。

translations.literal: Liu Yao entered through the Ximing Gate and encamped at the Armory.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao entered through the Ximing Gate and encamped at the Armory.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，曜殺太子詮、吳孝王晏、竟陵王楙、右僕射曹馥、尚書閭丘沖、河南尹劉默等，士民死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: On wuxu, Liu Yao killed the Crown Prince Quan, Liu Yan, Prince of Wu, Liu Mao, Prince of Jingling, Cao Fu, Right Vice Director, Luqiu Chong, Master of Writing, Liu Mo, Administrator of Henan, and others; more than thirty thousand soldiers and civilians died.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu, Liu Yao executed Crown Prince Quan, Liu Yan, Prince of Wu, Liu Mao, Prince of Jingling, Cao Fu, Right Vice Director, Luqiu Chong, Master of Writing, Liu Mo, Administrator of Henan, and many others; more than thirty thousand soldiers and civilians perished.

sentences.zh: 遂發掘諸陵，焚宮廟、官府皆盡。

translations.literal: He then excavated the imperial tombs and burned the palaces, temples, and government offices until nothing remained.
translations.idiomatic: He then opened the imperial tombs and burned the palaces, temples, and government offices until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 曜納惠帝羊皇后，遷帝及六璽於平陽。

translations.literal: Liu Yao took Empress Yang of Emperor Hui as his wife and moved the emperor and the six imperial seals to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao took Empress Yang of Emperor Hui into his household and removed the emperor and the six imperial seals to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 石勒引兵出轘轅，屯許昌。

translations.literal: Shi Le led troops out through Huanyuan and encamped at Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le marched out through Huanyuan Pass and encamped at Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 光祿大夫劉蕃、尚書盧志奔并州。

translations.literal: Liu Fan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Lu Zhi, Master of Writing, fled to Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fan, Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Lu Zhi, Master of Writing, fled to Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 丁未，漢主聰大赦，改元嘉平。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Han ruler Liu Cong proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jiaping.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Han ruler Liu Cong proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name to Jiaping.

sentences.zh: 以帝為特進左光祿大夫，封平阿公，以侍中庾鈱、王俊為光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He made the emperor Special Counselor and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed him as Duke of Ping'a; he made Yu Qian and Wang Jun, Attendants-in-Ordinary, Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He made the captive emperor Special Counselor and Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffing him as Duke of Ping'a; he appointed Yu Qian and Wang Jun, Attendants-in-Ordinary, as Grand Masters of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 鈱，敳之兄也。

translations.literal: Qian was the elder brother of Yu Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was the elder brother of Yu Yin.

sentences.zh: 初，始安王曜以王彌不待己至，先入洛陽，怨之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, resented Wang Mi because Wang Mi had entered Luoyang first without waiting for him to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, resented Wang Mi for entering Luoyang ahead of him without waiting for his arrival.

sentences.zh: 彌說曜曰：「洛陽天下之中，山河四塞，城池、宮室不假修營，宜白主上自平陽徙都之。」

translations.literal: Wang Mi urged Liu Yao, saying: "Luoyang is the center of the realm; mountains and rivers block it on four sides; its walls and palaces need no fresh construction—Your Highness should report to the sovereign that the capital should be moved here from Pingyang."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi urged Liu Yao: "Luoyang stands at the center of the realm, ringed by mountains and rivers on every side; its walls and palaces need no rebuilding. Your Highness should advise the sovereign to move the capital here from Pingyang."

sentences.zh: 曜以天下未定，洛陽四面受敵，不可守，不用彌策而焚之。

translations.literal: Liu Yao held that the realm was not yet settled, that Luoyang was exposed to attack on every side and could not be held, and so rejected Wang Mi's plan and burned the city.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao replied that the realm was not yet settled, that Luoyang lay exposed to attack on every side and could not be defended, and so he rejected Wang Mi's plan and burned the city.

sentences.zh: 彌罵曰：「屠各子，豈有帝王之意邪？」

translations.literal: Wang Mi cursed him, saying: "You son of the Tuge tribe—do you have any mind to be an emperor?"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi cursed him: "You whelp of the Tuge—have you any mind to be an emperor?"

sentences.zh: 遂與曜有隙，引兵東屯項關。

translations.literal: From this he and Liu Yao fell out; he led his troops east and encamped at Xiang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: From that point he and Liu Yao were estranged; Wang Mi led his troops east and encamped at Xiang Pass.

sentences.zh: 前司隸校尉劉暾說彌曰：「今九州糜沸，群雄競逐，將軍於漢建不世之功，又與始安王相失，將何以自容！

translations.literal: Liu Tan, former Colonel of the Metropolitan Area, urged Wang Mi, saying: "Now the Nine Provinces seethe like porridge and heroes vie in pursuit; the general has won unmatched merit for Han, yet you have fallen out with the Prince of Shi'an—how will you hold your place!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Tan, former Colonel of the Metropolitan Area, urged Wang Mi: "The Nine Provinces seethe and heroes vie for mastery; you have won unmatched merit for Han, yet you have quarreled with the Prince of Shi'an—how will you hold your place?

sentences.zh: 不如東據本州，徐觀天下之勢，上可以混壹四海，下不失鼎峙之業，策之上者也。」

translations.literal: Better to seize your home province in the east and watch the realm's trends at leisure: at best you may unite the four seas; at worst you will not lose the standing of a power that holds its ground—this is the highest strategy."
translations.idiomatic: Better to seize your home province in the east and watch how the realm unfolds: at best you may unite the four seas; at worst you will not lose the standing of a power that holds its ground—that is the highest strategy."

sentences.zh: 彌心然之。

translations.literal: Wang Mi was convinced in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi was convinced.

sentences.zh: 司徒傅祗建行臺於河陰，司空荀籓在陽城，河南尹華薈在成皋，汝陰太守平陽李矩為之立屋，輸穀以給之。

translations.literal: Grand Minister over the Masses Fu Zhi established a provisional court at Heyin; Minister of Works Xun Fan was at Yangcheng; Hua Hui, Administrator of Henan, was at Chenggao; Li Ju of Pingyang, Administrator of Runyin, built houses for them and sent grain to supply them.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Minister over the Masses Fu Zhi established a provisional court at Heyin; Minister of Works Xun Fan was at Yangcheng; Hua Hui, Administrator of Henan, was at Chenggao; Li Ju of Pingyang, Administrator of Runyin, built quarters for them and sent grain for their supply.

sentences.zh: 薈，歆之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Hui was the great-grandson of Hua Xin.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the great-grandson of Hua Xin.

sentences.zh: 籓與弟組、族子中護軍崧，薈與弟中領軍恆，建行台於密，傳檄四方，推琅邪王睿為盟主。

translations.literal: Xun Fan, together with his younger brother Zu and his clansman Xun Song, General of the Center Guard, and Hua Hui together with his younger brother Hua Heng, General of the Center Army, established a provisional court at Mi and issued proclamations in all directions, naming Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, as alliance leader.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan, with his younger brother Zu and his clansman Xun Song, General of the Center Guard, and Hua Hui with his younger brother Hua Heng, General of the Center Army, established a provisional court at Mi, issued proclamations in all directions, and named Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, as alliance leader.

sentences.zh: 籓承製以崧為襄城太守，矩為滎陽太守，前冠軍將軍河南褚翜為梁國內史。

translations.literal: Xun Fan, acting on provisional authority, made Xun Song Administrator of Xiangcheng, Li Ju Administrator of Xingyang, and Chu Shao of Henan, former Champion General, Interior Minister of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on provisional authority, Xun Fan appointed Xun Song Administrator of Xiangcheng, Li Ju Administrator of Xingyang, and Chu Shao of Henan, former Champion General, as Interior Minister of Liang.

sentences.zh: 揚威將軍魏浚屯洛北石樑塢，劉琨承制假浚河南尹，浚詣荀籓咨謀軍事。

translations.literal: Wei Jun, General Who Displays Might, encamped at the Shiliang Fort north of the Luo; Liu Kun, acting on provisional authority, made Wei Jun provisional Administrator of Henan; Wei Jun went to Xun Fan to consult on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jun, General Who Displays Might, held the Shiliang Fort north of the Luo; Liu Kun, acting on provisional authority, made Wei Jun provisional Administrator of Henan; Wei Jun went to Xun Fan to consult on military affairs.

sentences.zh: 籓邀李矩同會，矩夜赴之。

translations.literal: Xun Fan invited Li Ju to meet with him; Li Ju went by night to keep the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan invited Li Ju to a meeting; Li Ju went by night to keep the appointment.

sentences.zh: 矩官屬皆曰：「浚不可信，不宜夜往。」

translations.literal: Li Ju's staff all said: "Wei Jun cannot be trusted; you should not go by night."
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju's staff all said: "Wei Jun cannot be trusted—you should not go by night."

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「忠臣同心，何所疑乎！」

translations.literal: Li Ju said: "Loyal ministers share one heart—what is there to doubt!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Ju said: "Loyal ministers share one heart—what is there to doubt?"

sentences.zh: 遂往，相與結歡而去。

translations.literal: He went, and they joined in good fellowship and parted.
translations.idiomatic: He went; the two men joined in good fellowship and parted.

sentences.zh: 浚族子該，聚眾據一泉塢，籓以為武威將軍。

translations.literal: Wei Gai, a clansman of Wei Jun, gathered a force and held a spring fort; Xun Fan made him General of Martial Prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Gai, a clansman of Wei Jun, gathered followers and held a spring fort; Xun Fan made him General of Martial Prestige.

sentences.zh: 豫章王端，太子詮之弟也，東奔倉垣，苟晞率群官奉以為皇太子，置行臺。

translations.literal: Sima Duan, Prince of Yuzhang and younger brother of Crown Prince Quan, fled east to Cangyuan; Gou Xi led the officials in installing him as crown prince and established a provisional court.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Duan, Prince of Yuzhang and younger brother of Crown Prince Quan, fled east to Cangyuan; Gou Xi led the officials in installing him as crown prince and established a provisional court.

sentences.zh: 端承制以晞領太子太傅、都督中外諸軍、錄尚書事，自倉垣徙屯蒙城。

translations.literal: Duan, acting on provisional authority, made Gou Xi Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, Commander-in-Chief of all forces at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he moved his camp from Cangyuan to Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Acting on provisional authority, Duan made Gou Xi Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, Commander-in-Chief of all forces at home and abroad, and Recorder of the Masters of Writing; he moved his camp from Cangyuan to Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 撫軍將軍秦王業，吳孝王之子，荀籓之甥也，年十二，南奔密，籓等奉之，南趣許昌。

translations.literal: Sima Ye, Prince of Qin and General Who Pacifies the Army, son of Liu Yan, Prince of Wu, and nephew of Xun Fan, was twelve years old; he fled south to Mi; Xun Fan and the others escorted him and marched south toward Xuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ye, Prince of Qin and General Who Pacifies the Army, son of Liu Yan, Prince of Wu, and nephew of Xun Fan, was twelve years old; he fled south to Mi, and Xun Fan and the others escorted him south toward Xuchang.

sentences.zh: 前豫州刺史天水閻鼎，聚西州流民數千人於密，欲還鄉里。

translations.literal: Yan Ding of Tianshui, former Inspector of Yu Province, gathered several thousand refugees from the western provinces at Mi, intending to return to their home districts.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding of Tianshui, former Inspector of Yu Province, gathered several thousand refugees from the western provinces at Mi, intending to return to their home districts.

sentences.zh: 荀籓以鼎有才而擁眾，用鼎為豫州刺史，以中書令李絲亙、司徒左長史彭城劉疇、鎮軍長史周顗、司馬李述等為之參佐。

translations.literal: Xun Fan, because Yan Ding had talent and commanded a following, made him Inspector of Yu Province and appointed Li Sigen, Director of the Masters of Writing, Liu Chou of Pengcheng, Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Minister over the Masses, Zhou Yi, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Army, Li Shu, Army Major, and others as his aides.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan Ding had talent and commanded a following, Xun Fan made him Inspector of Yu Province and appointed Li Sigen, Director of the Masters of Writing, Liu Chou of Pengcheng, Left Chief Clerk of the Grand Minister over the Masses, Zhou Yi, Chief Clerk of the Pacifying Army, Li Shu, Army Major, and others as his aides.

sentences.zh: 顗，浚之子也。

translations.literal: Yi was the son of Zhou Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was the son of Zhou Jun.

sentences.zh: 時海內大亂，獨江東差安，中國士民避亂者多南渡江。

translations.literal: At this time the realm was in great disorder, but the lands east of the Yangzi alone were somewhat secure; many gentry and commoners of the Central Plains fled south across the river to escape the chaos.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the realm was in great disorder, but the lands east of the Yangzi alone were somewhat secure; many gentry and commoners of the Central Plains fled south across the river to escape the chaos.

sentences.zh: 鎮東司馬王導說琅邪王睿收其賢俊，與之共事。

translations.literal: Wang Dao, Major of the Pacifying Army, urged Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, to gather their worthy and outstanding men and work with them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao, Major of the Pacifying Army, urged Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, to gather the talented and outstanding among them and work with them.

sentences.zh: 睿從之，辟手彖屬百餘人，時人謂之百六手彖。

translations.literal: Rui followed his advice and recruited more than a hundred scribe-clerks; contemporaries called them the Hundred-Six Scribes.
translations.idiomatic: Rui followed his advice and recruited more than a hundred scribe-clerks; contemporaries dubbed them the Hundred-Six Scribes.

sentences.zh: 以前穎川太守勃海刁協為軍咨祭酒，前東海太守王承、廣陵相卞壺為從事中郎，江寧令諸葛恢、歷陽參軍陳國陳頵為行參軍，前太傅手彖庚亮為西曹手彖。

translations.literal: He made Diao Xie of Bohai, former Administrator of Yingchuan, Military Adviser and Sacrificial Officer; Wang Cheng, former Administrator of Donghai, and Bian Hu, Chancellor of Guangling, Gentlemen of Attendance; Zhuge Hui, Magistrate of Jiangning, and Chen Yin of Chen, Staff Officer of Liyang, Traveling Staff Officers; and Geng Liang, former scribe of the Grand Tutor, Western Bureau Scribe.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Diao Xie of Bohai, former Administrator of Yingchuan, as Military Adviser and Sacrificial Officer; Wang Cheng, former Administrator of Donghai, and Bian Hu, Chancellor of Guangling, as Gentlemen of Attendance; Zhuge Hui, Magistrate of Jiangning, and Chen Yin of Chen, Staff Officer of Liyang, as Traveling Staff Officers; and Geng Liang, former scribe of the Grand Tutor, as Western Bureau Scribe.

sentences.zh: 承，渾之弟子；

translations.literal: Cheng was a nephew of Wang Hun;
translations.idiomatic: Cheng was a nephew of Wang Hun;

sentences.zh: 恢，靚之子；

translations.literal: Hui was the son of Zhuge Jing;
translations.idiomatic: Hui was the son of Zhuge Jing;

sentences.zh: 亮，兗之弟子也。

translations.literal: Liang was a nephew of Geng Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was a nephew of Geng Yan.

sentences.zh: 江州刺史華軼，歆之間孫也，自以受朝廷之命而為琅邪王睿所督，多不受其教令。

translations.literal: Hua Yi, Inspector of Jiang Province and great-great-grandson of Hua Xin, considered himself appointed by the court yet subject to the supervision of Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, and often refused to obey his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yi, Inspector of Jiang Province and great-great-grandson of Hua Xin, considered himself appointed by the court yet subject to the supervision of Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, and often refused to obey his orders.

sentences.zh: 郡縣多諫之，軼曰：「吾欲見詔書耳。」

translations.literal: Many in the commanderies and counties remonstrated with him; Yi said: "I wish only to see an imperial edict."
translations.idiomatic: Many in the commanderies and counties remonstrated with him; Yi said: "I wish only to see an imperial edict."

sentences.zh: 及睿承荀籓檄，承製署置官司，改易長吏，軼與豫州刺史裴憲皆不從命。

translations.literal: When Rui, acting on Xun Fan's proclamation, assumed provisional authority to appoint officials and replace local administrators, both Yi and Pei Xian, Inspector of Yu Province, refused to obey.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui, acting on Xun Fan's proclamation, assumed provisional authority to appoint officials and replace local administrators, both Yi and Pei Xian, Inspector of Yu Province, refused to obey.

sentences.zh: 睿遣揚州刺史王敦、歷陽內史甘卓與揚烈將軍廬江周訪合兵擊軼。

translations.literal: Rui sent Wang Dun, Inspector of Yang Province, Gan Zhuo, Interior Minister of Liyang, and Zhou Fang of Lujiang, General of Fierce Might, to combine forces and attack Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent Wang Dun, Inspector of Yang Province, Gan Zhuo, Interior Minister of Liyang, and Zhou Fang of Lujiang, General of Fierce Might, to combine forces and attack Yi.

sentences.zh: 軼兵敗，奔安成，訪追斬之，及其五子。

translations.literal: Yi's army was defeated; he fled to Ancheng; Zhou Fang pursued and executed him, together with his five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's army was defeated; he fled to Ancheng; Zhou Fang pursued and executed him, together with his five sons.

sentences.zh: 裴憲奔幽州。

translations.literal: Pei Xian fled to You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xian fled to You Province.

sentences.zh: 睿以甘卓為湘州刺史，周訪為尋陽太守，又以揚武將軍陶侃為武昌太守。

translations.literal: Rui made Gan Zhuo Inspector of Xiang Province, Zhou Fang Administrator of Xunyang, and Tao Kan, General of Martial Prestige, Administrator of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: Rui made Gan Zhuo Inspector of Xiang Province, Zhou Fang Administrator of Xunyang, and Tao Kan, General of Martial Prestige, Administrator of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，王浚設壇告類，立皇太子，佈告天下，稱受中詔承制封拜，備置百官，列署征、鎮，以荀籓為太尉，琅邪王睿為大將軍。

translations.literal: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wang Jun set up an altar and reported to Heaven, installed a crown prince, and proclaimed it to the realm, declaring that he had received an edict from within the palace to assume provisional authority for enfeoffments and appointments; he fully established the bureaucracy and posted generals and commanders; he made Xun Fan Grand Commandant and Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, in the seventh month, Wang Jun set up an altar and reported to Heaven, installed a crown prince, and proclaimed it to the realm, declaring that he had received an edict from within the palace to assume provisional authority for enfeoffments and appointments; he fully established the bureaucracy and posted generals and commanders, making Xun Fan Grand Commandant and Sima Rui, Prince of Langye, Grand General.

sentences.zh: 浚自領尚書令，以裴憲及其婿棗嵩為尚書，以田征為兗州刺史，李惲為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Wang Jun himself took charge as Director of the Masters of Writing; he made Pei Xian and his son-in-law Zao Song Masters of Writing; he made Tian Zheng Inspector of Yan Province and Li Yun Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun himself took charge as Director of the Masters of Writing; he made Pei Xian and his son-in-law Zao Song Masters of Writing; he made Tian Zheng Inspector of Yan Province and Li Yun Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 南陽王模使牙門趙染戍薄板，染求馮翊太守不得而怒，帥眾降漢，漢主聰以染為平西將軍。

translations.literal: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, had his gate officer Zhao Ran garrison Bo Gate; Ran, angry that he was not made Administrator of Fufeng, led his followers in surrendering to Han; Han ruler Liu Cong made Ran General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, had his gate officer Zhao Ran garrison Bo Gate; Ran, angry at not being made Administrator of Fufeng, led his followers in surrendering to Han; Han ruler Liu Cong made Ran General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 八月，聰遣染與安西將軍劉雅帥騎二萬攻模於長安，河內王粲、始安王曜帥大眾繼之。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Liu Cong sent Ran together with Liu Ya, General Who Pacifies the West, leading twenty thousand cavalry to attack Mo at Chang'an; Liu Can, Prince of Henei, and Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, followed with a great host.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Liu Cong sent Ran together with Liu Ya, General Who Pacifies the West, leading twenty thousand cavalry to attack Mo at Chang'an; Liu Can, Prince of Henei, and Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, followed with a great host.

sentences.zh: 染敗模兵於潼關，長驅至下邽。

translations.literal: Ran defeated Mo's army at Tong Pass and drove straight to Xia Gui.
translations.idiomatic: Ran defeated Mo's army at Tong Pass and drove straight to Xia Gui.

sentences.zh: 涼州將北宮純自長安帥其眾降漢。

translations.literal: Beigong Chun, a general of Liang Province, led his followers from Chang'an in surrendering to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Beigong Chun, a general of Liang Province, led his followers from Chang'an in surrendering to Han.

sentences.zh: 漢兵圍長安，模遣淳於定出戰而敗。

translations.literal: Han troops besieged Chang'an; Mo sent Chunyu Ding out to give battle and was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops besieged Chang'an; Mo sent Chunyu Ding out to give battle and was defeated.

sentences.zh: 模倉庫虛竭，士卒離散，遂降於漢。

translations.literal: Mo's storehouses were empty and exhausted, his soldiers scattered, and he surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Mo's storehouses were empty, his soldiers scattered, and he surrendered to Han.

sentences.zh: 趙染送模於河內王粲；

translations.literal: Zhao Ran escorted Mo to Liu Can, Prince of Henei;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ran escorted Mo to Liu Can, Prince of Henei;

sentences.zh: 九月，粲殺模。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Liu Can executed Mo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, Liu Can executed Mo.

sentences.zh: 關西饑饉，白骨蔽野，士民存者百無一二。

translations.literal: In the lands west of the Pass famine raged; white bones covered the fields, and scarcely one or two in a hundred of the gentry and commoners survived.
translations.idiomatic: In the lands west of the Pass famine raged; white bones covered the fields, and scarcely one or two in a hundred of the gentry and commoners survived.

sentences.zh: 聰以始安王曜為車騎大將軍、雍州牧，更封中山王，鎮長安。

translations.literal: Liu Cong made Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yong Province, changed his fief to Prince of Zhongshan, and stationed him at Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong made Liu Yao, Prince of Shi'an, General of Chariots and Cavalry and Governor of Yong Province, changed his fief to Prince of Zhongshan, and stationed him at Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 以王彌為大將軍，封齊公。

translations.literal: He made Wang Mi Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He made Wang Mi Grand General and enfeoffed him as Duke of Qi.

sentences.zh: 苟晞驕奢苛暴，前遼西太守閻亨，纘之子也，數諫晞，晞殺之。

translations.literal: Gou Xi was arrogant, extravagant, harsh, and violent; Yan Heng, former Administrator of Liaoxi and son of Yan Ji, repeatedly remonstrated with him, and Gou Xi killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi was arrogant, extravagant, harsh, and violent; Yan Heng, former Administrator of Liaoxi and son of Yan Ji, repeatedly remonstrated with him, and Gou Xi killed him.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎明預有疾，自輿入諫。

translations.literal: Ming Yu, Attendant Gentleman, was ill and had himself carried in a litter to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Yu, Attendant Gentleman, was ill and had himself carried in a litter to remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 晞怒曰：「我殺閻亨，何關人事，而輿病罵我！」

translations.literal: Gou Xi said in anger: "I killed Yan Heng—what business is that of other men, that you come in a sick litter to revile me!"
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi said in anger: "I killed Yan Heng—what business is that of other men, that you come in a sick litter to revile me?"

sentences.zh: 預曰：「明公以禮待預，故預以禮自盡。

translations.literal: Yu said: "Your Excellency treated Yu with courtesy, so Yu answered with courtesy to the full.
translations.idiomatic: Yu said: "Your Excellency treated me with courtesy, so I answered with courtesy to the full.

sentences.zh: 今明公怒預，其如遠近怒明公何！
