translations.literal: Now Your Excellency is angry with Yu—what of the anger of men near and far at Your Excellency!
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Excellency is angry with me—what of the anger of men near and far at Your Excellency?

sentences.zh: 桀為天子，猶以驕暴而亡，況人臣乎！

translations.literal: Jie was Son of Heaven yet still perished through arrogance and violence—how much more a subject!
translations.idiomatic: Jie was Son of Heaven yet still perished through arrogance and violence—how much more a subject!

sentences.zh: 願明公且置是怒，思預之言。」

translations.literal: I beg Your Excellency for the moment to set aside this anger and consider Yu's words."
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Excellency to set aside this anger for the moment and consider my words."

sentences.zh: 晞不從。

translations.literal: Gou Xi did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi did not listen.

sentences.zh: 由是眾心離怨，加以疾疫、饑饉。

translations.literal: From this the hearts of the multitude turned away in resentment, and pestilence and famine were added besides.
translations.idiomatic: From this the hearts of the multitude turned away in resentment, and pestilence and famine were added besides.

sentences.zh: 石勒攻王贊於陽夏，擒之。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Wang Zan at Yangxia and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Wang Zan at Yangxia and captured him.

sentences.zh: 遂襲蒙城，執及豫章王晞端，鎖晞頸，以為左司馬。

translations.literal: He then raided Mengcheng, seized Gou Xi and Sima Duan, Prince of Yuzhang, put a collar on Gou Xi's neck, and made him Left Major.
translations.idiomatic: He then raided Mengcheng, seized Gou Xi and Sima Duan, Prince of Yuzhang, put a collar on Gou Xi's neck, and made him Left Major.

sentences.zh: 漢主聰拜勒幽州牧。

translations.literal: Han ruler Liu Cong appointed Shi Le Governor of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: Han ruler Liu Cong appointed Shi Le Governor of You Province.

sentences.zh: 王彌與勒，外相親而內相忌，劉暾說彌使召曹嶷之兵以圖勒，彌為書，使暾召嶷，且邀勒兵共向青州。

translations.literal: Wang Mi and Shi Le were outwardly friendly yet inwardly suspicious of each other; Liu Tan urged Wang Mi to summon Cao Ni's troops to plot against Shi Le; Wang Mi wrote a letter, had Liu Tan summon Cao Ni, and also invited Shi Le's troops to march together toward Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi and Shi Le were outwardly friendly yet inwardly suspicious of each other; Liu Tan urged Wang Mi to summon Cao Ni's troops to plot against Shi Le; Wang Mi wrote a letter, had Liu Tan summon Cao Ni, and also invited Shi Le's troops to march together toward Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 暾至東阿，勒游騎獲之，勒潛殺暾而彌不知。

translations.literal: When Liu Tan reached Dong'e, Shi Le's patrol riders captured him; Shi Le secretly killed Liu Tan, and Wang Mi did not know.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Tan reached Dong'e, Shi Le's patrol riders captured him; Shi Le secretly killed Liu Tan, and Wang Mi knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 會彌將徐邈、高梁輒引所部兵去，彌兵漸衰。

translations.literal: Just then Wang Mi's generals Xu Miao and Gao Liangzhe led their own units away; Wang Mi's army gradually weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Mi's generals Xu Miao and Gao Liangzhe led their own units away; Wang Mi's army gradually weakened.

sentences.zh: 彌聞勒擒苟晞，心惡之，以書賀勒曰：「公獲苟晞而用之，何其神也！

translations.literal: When Wang Mi heard that Shi Le had captured Gou Xi, he was displeased at heart and wrote to congratulate Shi Le, saying: "Your Lordship captured Gou Xi and put him to use—how divine!
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mi heard that Shi Le had captured Gou Xi, he was displeased at heart and wrote to congratulate Shi Le: "Your Lordship captured Gou Xi and put him to use—how inspired!

sentences.zh: 使晞為公左，彌為公右，天下不足定也。」

translations.literal: Let Gou Xi be Your Lordship's left hand and Mi Your Lordship's right—the realm would not be hard to settle."
translations.idiomatic: Let Gou Xi be your left hand and Mi your right—the realm would not be hard to settle."

sentences.zh: 勒謂張賓曰：「王公位重而言卑，其圖我必矣。」

translations.literal: Shi Le said to Zhang Bin: "Lord Wang holds high rank yet speaks humbly—he surely plots against me."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le said to Zhang Bin: "Lord Wang holds high rank yet speaks humbly—he surely plots against me."

sentences.zh: 賓因勸勒乘彌小衰，誘而取之。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin therefore urged Shi Le to take advantage of Wang Mi's slight decline and lure him in and seize him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin therefore urged Shi Le to take advantage of Wang Mi's slight decline, lure him in, and seize him.

sentences.zh: 時勒方與乞活陳午相攻於蓬關，彌亦與劉瑞相持甚急。

translations.literal: At this time Shi Le was attacking Chen Wu of the Qihuo at Peng Pass, and Wang Mi was also locked in fierce combat with Liu Rui.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Shi Le was attacking Chen Wu of the Qihuo at Peng Pass, and Wang Mi was also locked in fierce combat with Liu Rui.

sentences.zh: 彌請救於勒，勒未之許。

translations.literal: Wang Mi asked Shi Le for rescue; Shi Le did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi asked Shi Le for rescue; Shi Le did not agree.

sentences.zh: 張賓曰：「公常恐不得王公之便，今天以王公授我矣。

translations.literal: Zhang Bin said: "Your Lordship has always feared that you would not get a chance at Lord Wang—today Heaven has delivered Lord Wang to us.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bin said: "Your Lordship has always feared that you would not get a chance at Lord Wang—today Heaven has delivered Lord Wang to us.

sentences.zh: 陳午小豎，不足憂；

translations.literal: Chen Wu is a mere stripling—not worth worry;
translations.idiomatic: Chen Wu is a mere stripling—not worth worrying over;

sentences.zh: 王公人傑，當早除之。」

translations.literal: Lord Wang is a man of heroic stature and should be removed early."
translations.idiomatic: Lord Wang is a man of heroic stature and should be removed early."

sentences.zh: 勒乃引兵擊瑞，斬之。

translations.literal: Shi Le then led troops to attack Liu Rui and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le then led troops to attack Liu Rui and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 彌大喜，謂勒實親己，不復疑也。

translations.literal: Wang Mi was greatly pleased, believing that Shi Le was truly friendly to him, and no longer harbored suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi was greatly pleased, believing that Shi Le was truly friendly to him, and no longer harbored suspicion.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，勒請彌燕於己吾。

translations.literal: In winter, in the tenth month, Shi Le invited Wang Mi to a banquet at Jiwu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, in the tenth month, Shi Le invited Wang Mi to a banquet at Jiwu.

sentences.zh: 彌將往，長史張嵩諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Wang Mi was about to go; Zhang Song, Chief Clerk, remonstrated, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mi was about to go; Zhang Song, Chief Clerk, remonstrated, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，勒手斬彌而並其眾，表漢主聰，稱彌叛逆。

translations.literal: When the wine had gone deep, Shi Le personally beheaded Wang Mi and absorbed his followers; he memorialized Han ruler Liu Cong, declaring that Wang Mi had rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine had gone deep, Shi Le personally beheaded Wang Mi and absorbed his followers; he memorialized Han ruler Liu Cong, declaring that Wang Mi had rebelled.

sentences.zh: 聰大怒，遣使讓勒「專害公輔，有無君之心」，然猶加勒鎮東大將軍、督並、幽二州諸軍事、領并州刺史，以慰其心。

translations.literal: Liu Cong was greatly angered and sent an envoy to rebuke Shi Le for "killing a high minister on his own authority, harboring a heart without a lord," yet still added to Shi Le's titles as General Who Pacifies the East, Commander of all military affairs in Bing and You provinces, and concurrent Inspector of Bing Province, to soothe his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Cong was greatly angered and sent an envoy to rebuke Shi Le for "killing a high minister on his own authority, harboring a heart without a lord," yet still added to Shi Le's titles as General Who Pacifies the East, Commander of all military affairs in Bing and You provinces, and concurrent Inspector of Bing Province, to soothe his heart.

sentences.zh: 苟晞、王贊潛謀叛勒，勒殺之，並晞弟純。

translations.literal: Gou Xi and Wang Zan secretly plotted to rebel against Shi Le; Shi Le executed them and also Gou Xi's younger brother Chun.
translations.idiomatic: Gou Xi and Wang Zan secretly plotted to rebel against Shi Le; Shi Le executed them and also Gou Xi's younger brother Chun.

sentences.zh: 勒引兵掠豫州諸郡，臨江而還，屯於葛陂。

translations.literal: Shi Le led troops to plunder the commanderies of Yu Province, reached the river, and returned; he encamped at Gebei.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le led troops to plunder the commanderies of Yu Province, reached the river, and returned; he encamped at Gebei.

sentences.zh: 初，勒之為人所掠賣也，與其母王氏相失。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Shi Le had been captured and sold by others, he and his mother Lady Wang were separated.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shi Le had been captured and sold into bondage, he and his mother Lady Wang were separated.

sentences.zh: 劉琨得之，並其從子虎送於勒，因遺勒書曰：「將軍用兵如神，所向無敵。

translations.literal: Liu Kun captured her and, together with Shi Le's nephew Hu, sent them to Shi Le; he also sent Shi Le a letter, saying: "The general's use of troops is divine, and none can stand before you.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun captured her and, together with Shi Le's nephew Hu, sent them to Shi Le; he also sent Shi Le a letter: "The general's use of troops is divine, and none can stand before you.

sentences.zh: 所以周流天下而無容足之地，百戰百勝而無尺寸之功者，蓋得主則為義兵，附逆則為賊眾故也。

translations.literal: The reason you roam the realm yet have no place to set foot, win a hundred battles yet gain no measure of merit, is simply that when you hold to a true lord you are a righteous army, but when you attach yourself to rebels you become a band of brigands.
translations.idiomatic: The reason you roam the realm yet have nowhere to stand, win a hundred battles yet gain no measure of merit, is simply this: when you serve a true lord you are a righteous army, but when you attach yourself to rebels you become a band of brigands.

sentences.zh: 成敗之數，有似呼吸，吹之則寒，噓之則溫。

translations.literal: The tally of victory and defeat is like breathing: blow on it and it turns cold; breathe warmly on it and it turns warm.
translations.idiomatic: Fortune in victory and defeat shifts like breath on the skin—a puff and one grows cold, a warm exhale and one grows warm.

sentences.zh: 今相授侍中、車騎大將軍、領護匈奴中郎將、襄城郡公，將軍其受之！」

translations.literal: Now I hereby confer on you the posts of Attendant Within, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, acting Protector of the Xiongnu Commandant, and Duke of Xiangcheng Commandery—General, accept them!"
translations.idiomatic: I now confer on you Attendant Within, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, Protector of the Xiongnu Commandant, and Duke of Xiangcheng—General, accept these offices!"

sentences.zh: 勒報書曰：「事功殊途，非腐儒所知。

translations.literal: Shi Le replied in writing: "Achievement and duty follow different paths—not something pedantic scholars can understand.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le wrote back: "Merit and duty follow different paths—beyond what bookish pedants can grasp.

sentences.zh: 君當逞節本朝，吾自夷難為效。」

translations.literal: You should exert your integrity in service of your own dynasty; I for my part will eliminate hardships as my contribution."
translations.idiomatic: You should hold fast to your integrity in your own dynasty's service; I for my part will settle turmoil as my contribution."

sentences.zh: 遺琨名馬、珍寶，厚禮其使，謝而絕之。

translations.literal: He sent Kun famous horses and precious treasures, treated his envoy with great courtesy, and declined while expressing thanks.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Kun fine horses and precious treasures, lavished gifts on his envoy, thanked him—and refused.

sentences.zh: 時虎年十七，殘忍無度，為軍中患。

translations.literal: At the time Hu was seventeen years old, cruel beyond measure, a scourge in the army.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Hu was seventeen—cruel beyond all bounds and a plague upon the army.

sentences.zh: 勒白母曰：「此兒凶暴無賴，使軍人殺之，聲名可惜，不若自除之。」

translations.literal: Shi Le said to his mother: "This boy is fierce, violent, and unrestrained. Having the soldiers kill him would waste my good name—it is better that I dispose of him myself."
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le told his mother: "This boy is savage and utterly lawless. If I had the soldiers kill him, my reputation would suffer—it is better I remove him myself."

sentences.zh: 母曰：「快牛為犢，多能破車，汝小忍之！」

translations.literal: His mother said: "A spirited ox bears a calf that often wrecks the cart—bear with him a little!"
translations.idiomatic: His mother said: "A spirited ox sires a calf that often wrecks the cart—bear with him awhile!"

sentences.zh: 及長，便弓馬，勇冠當時。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he became skilled with bow and horse, and his courage surpassed all of his age.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age, he mastered bow and horse, and his courage outstripped every man of his generation.

sentences.zh: 勒以為征虜將軍，每屠城邑，鮮有遺類。

translations.literal: Shi Le made him General Who Conquers Barbarians; whenever cities were sacked, scarcely anyone survived.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le made him General Who Conquers Barbarians; whenever a city fell to him, scarcely a soul was left alive.

sentences.zh: 然御眾嚴而不煩，莫敢犯者，指授攻討，所向無前，勒遂寵任之。

translations.literal: Yet in commanding troops he was stern without being vexatious—none dared defy him; when he directed attacks, nowhere could stand before him, and Shi Le came to favor and trust him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in command he was stern without being burdensome—none dared cross him; wherever he directed an assault, nothing stood before him, and Shi Le came to favor and rely on him.

sentences.zh: 勒攻滎陽太守李矩，矩擊卻之。

translations.literal: Shi Le attacked Li Ju, Administrator of Xingyang; Ju drove him back.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le attacked Li Ju, Administrator of Xingyang; Ju beat him back.

sentences.zh: 初，南陽王模以從事中郎綝為馮翊太守。

translations.literal: Earlier, Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, had appointed Suo Lin, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Fengyi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Sima Mo, Prince of Nanyang, had made Suo Lin, Attendant of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Fengyi.

sentences.zh: 綝，靖之子也。

translations.literal: Suo Lin was Suo Jing's son.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Lin was Suo Jing's son.

sentences.zh: 模死，綝與安夷護軍金城麴允、頻陽令梁肅，俱奔安定。

translations.literal: After Mo died, Suo Lin fled to Anding together with Qu Yun of Jincheng, Protector of Anyi, and Liang Su, Magistrate of Pinyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Mo died, Suo Lin fled to Anding with Qu Yun of Jincheng, Protector of Anyi, and Liang Su, Magistrate of Pinyang.

sentences.zh: 時安定太守賈疋與諸氐、羌皆送任子於漢，綝等遇之於陰密，擁還臨涇，與疋謀興復晉室，疋從之。

translations.literal: At the time Jia Pi, Administrator of Anding, along with various Di and Qiang tribes, were all sending hostages to Han; Suo Lin and the others encountered them at Yinmi, compelled them to turn back to Linjing, and joined Pi in plotting to restore the Jin dynasty—Pi agreed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jia Pi, Administrator of Anding, and various Di and Qiang chiefs were all sending hostages to Han; Suo Lin and his party met them at Yinmi, forced them back to Linjing, and joined Pi in plotting to restore the Jin dynasty—Pi agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃共推疋為平西將軍，帥眾五萬向長安。

translations.literal: They jointly made Pi General Who Pacifies the West and led fifty thousand men toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: They jointly made Pi General Who Pacifies the West and marched fifty thousand men on Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 雍州刺史麴特、新平太守竺恢皆不降於漢，聞疋起兵，與扶風太守梁綜帥眾十萬會之。

translations.literal: Qu Te, Inspector of Yong Province, and Zhu Hui, Administrator of Xinping, had both refused to submit to Han; hearing that Pi had risen, they joined with Liang Zong, Administrator of Fufeng, leading a hundred thousand men to unite with him.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Te, Inspector of Yong Province, and Zhu Hui, Administrator of Xinping, had both refused to submit to Han; when they heard Pi had risen, they joined Liang Zong, Administrator of Fufeng, at the head of a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 綜，肅之兄也。

translations.literal: Liang Zong was Liang Su's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Zong was Liang Su's elder brother.

sentences.zh: 漢河內王粲在新豐，使其將劉雅、趙染攻新平，不克。

translations.literal: Wang Can, Prince of Henei of Han, was at Xinfeng; he sent his generals Liu Ya and Zhao Ran to attack Xinping but they failed to take it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Can, Prince of Henei of Han, was at Xinfeng; he sent Liu Ya and Zhao Ran against Xinping, but they could not take it.

sentences.zh: 索綝救新平，大小百戰，雅等敗退。

translations.literal: Suo Lin relieved Xinping; after a hundred engagements great and small, Liu Ya and the others were defeated and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Suo Lin relieved Xinping; after a hundred battles large and small, Liu Ya and the others were beaten back.

sentences.zh: 中山王曜與疋等戰於黃丘，曜眾大敗。

translations.literal: Liu Yao, Prince of Zhongshan, fought Jia Pi and the others at Huangqiu; Yao's forces suffered a crushing defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yao, Prince of Zhongshan, fought Jia Pi and his allies at Huangqiu; Yao's army was routed.

sentences.zh: 疋遂襲漢梁州刺史彭蕩仲，殺之。

translations.literal: Pi then raided Peng Dangzhong, Han Governor of Liang Province, and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pi then struck Peng Dangzhong, Han Governor of Liang Province, and killed him.

sentences.zh: 麴特等擊破粲於新豐，粲還平陽。

translations.literal: Qu Te and the others routed Wang Can at Xinfeng, and Can withdrew to Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Qu Te and the others routed Wang Can at Xinfeng, and Can fell back to Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 於是疋等兵勢大振，關西胡、晉翕然響應。

translations.literal: Thereupon the forces under Pi and the others surged mightily, and Hu and Jin throughout the Guanxi region rallied to them in rapid succession.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Pi and his allies grew mighty in arms, and Hu and Jin throughout the Guanxi region rallied to them as one.

sentences.zh: 閻鼎欲奉秦王業入關，據長安以號令四方；

translations.literal: Yan Ding wished to escort Ye, Prince of Qin, into the passes, seize Chang'an, and from there command the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Yan Ding wished to escort Ye, Prince of Qin, through the passes, hold Chang'an, and from there command the realm;

sentences.zh: 河陰令傅暢，祗之子也，亦以書勸之，鼎遂行。

translations.literal: Fu Chang, Magistrate of Heyin—Fu Zhi's son—also urged this course in a letter, and Ding set out.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang, Magistrate of Heyin—Fu Zhi's son—also urged it in a letter, and Ding set out.

sentences.zh: 荀籓、劉疇、周敳、李述等，皆山東人，不欲西行，中途逃散；

translations.literal: Xun Fan, Liu Chou, Zhou Yi, Li Shu, and others were all men of Shandong and did not wish to go west; midway they fled and scattered;
translations.idiomatic: Xun Fan, Liu Chou, Zhou Yi, Li Shu, and the rest were all men of Shandong and did not wish to go west; midway they broke away and fled;

sentences.zh: 鼎遣兵追之，不及，殺李絲亙等。

translations.literal: Ding sent troops in pursuit but could not overtake them; he killed Li Sigeng and others.
translations.idiomatic: Ding sent troops after them but could not catch them; he killed Li Sigeng and others.

sentences.zh: 鼎與業自宛趣武關，遇盜於上洛，士卒敗散，收其餘眾，進至藍田，使人告賈疋，疋遣兵迎之；

translations.literal: Ding and Ye set out from Wan toward Wuguan; at Shangluo they encountered bandits, and the soldiers were routed and scattered; gathering the remnant force, they advanced to Lantian and sent word to Jia Pi, who dispatched troops to welcome them;
translations.idiomatic: Ding and Ye marched from Wan toward Wuguan; at Shangluo they met bandits and the troops were routed; gathering what remained, they pressed on to Lantian and sent word to Jia Pi, who dispatched troops to meet them;

sentences.zh: 十二月，入於雍城，使梁綜將兵衛之。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month they entered Yong City; Liang Zong was assigned to garrison and guard them with troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month they entered Yong City; Liang Zong was put in command of the troops guarding them.

sentences.zh: 周顗奔琅邪王睿，睿以顗為軍諮祭酒。

translations.literal: Zhou Yi fled to Sima Rui, Prince of Langya; Rui made Yi Army Advisor and Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Yi fled to Sima Rui, Prince of Langya; Rui made him Army Advisor and Libationer.

sentences.zh: 前騎都尉譙國桓彝亦避亂過江，見睿微弱，謂敳曰：「我以中州多故，來此求全，而單弱如此，將何以濟！」

translations.literal: Former Commandant of the Rapid Cavalry Huan Yi of Qiao also fled the turmoil and crossed the Yangtze; seeing how weak Rui was, he said to Zhou Yi: "I came here seeking safety because the Central Plains are in such turmoil—and yet we are this feeble; how shall we prevail!"
translations.idiomatic: Former Commandant of the Rapid Cavalry Huan Yi of Qiao also fled the chaos and crossed the Yangtze; seeing how weak Rui was, he said to Zhou Yi: "I came south seeking refuge because the Central Plains are in turmoil—and yet we are this feeble; how can we succeed!"

sentences.zh: 既而見王導，共論世事，退，謂顗曰：「向見管夷吾，無復憂矣！」

translations.literal: Later he met Wang Dao and they discussed affairs of the age together; afterward, returning, he said to Zhou Yi: "Just now I met a Guan Zhong—I have no further worries!"
translations.idiomatic: Later he met Wang Dao and they talked over the state of the realm; on his return he said to Zhou Yi: "I have just met a Guan Zhong—there is nothing left to worry about!"

sentences.zh: 諸名士相與登新亭游宴，周顗中坐歎曰：「風景不殊，舉目有江河之異！」

translations.literal: The eminent scholars gathered to ascend the New Pavilion for a feast and outing; Zhou Yi, seated among them, sighed and said: "The scenery is no different, yet lifting one's eyes one sees the rivers and mountains have changed!"
translations.idiomatic: The leading scholars gathered at the New Pavilion for a feast; Zhou Yi, seated among them, sighed and said: "The view is unchanged, yet everywhere one looks the rivers and mountains are not the same!"

sentences.zh: 因相視流涕。

translations.literal: And at that they looked at one another and wept.
translations.idiomatic: At that they looked at one another and wept.

sentences.zh: 王導愀然變色曰：「當共戮力王室，克復神州，何至作楚囚對泣邪！」

translations.literal: Wang Dao's face fell and his expression changed as he said: "We should join our strength for the royal house and reconquer the Central Realm—how can we play captive men of Chu weeping face to face!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dao's face darkened as he said: "We should join our strength for the royal house and reconquer the Central Realm—why act like captive men of Chu, weeping in each other's faces!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆收淚謝之。

translations.literal: All then wiped away their tears and apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: All wiped away their tears and apologized to him.

sentences.zh: 陳頵遺王導書曰：「中華所以傾弊者，正以取才失所，先白望而後實事，浮競驅馳，互相貢薦，言重者先顯，言輕者後敘，遂相波扇，乃至陵遲。

translations.literal: Chen Yin sent Wang Dao a letter: "The reason the Central States have collapsed is precisely that talent has been misplaced: empty reputation comes first, solid achievement afterward; the ambitious race one another in vain display, recommending each other in turn—those whose words carry weight rise first, those whose words carry less are ranked later—until the fashion spread and decay set in.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yin wrote Wang Dao: "The Central States collapsed because talent was misplaced—empty reputation came first, real achievement afterward; men raced one another in vain ambition, trading recommendations back and forth; those whose words carried weight rose first, those whose words weighed less came later—until the fashion spread and the realm sank into ruin.

sentences.zh: 加有莊、老之俗，傾惑朝廷，養望者為弘雅，政事者為俗人，王職不恤，法物墜喪。

translations.literal: To this was added the fashion for Zhuangzi and Laozi, which misled the court: those who cultivated reputation were called refined and elegant, those who handled affairs were called vulgar men—the royal duties went untended, and the institutions of state fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: On top of this came the Zhuangzi–Laozi fashion, which bewitched the court: those who cultivated reputation passed for refined elegance, those who handled affairs were dismissed as vulgar—royal duties went untended and the institutions of state crumbled.

sentences.zh: 夫欲制遠，先由近始。

translations.literal: To govern what is distant, one must begin with what is near.
translations.idiomatic: To govern what is distant, one must begin with what is near.

sentences.zh: 今宜改張，明賞信罰，拔卓茂於密縣，顯朱邑於桐鄉，然後大業可舉，中興可冀耳。」

translations.literal: Now the policy should be changed: rewards and punishments made clear and trustworthy; a Zhuo Mao should be raised up from Miyi County, a Zhu Yi displayed at Tongxiang—then the great enterprise can be undertaken and restoration may be hoped for."
translations.idiomatic: Now the policy must change—rewards and punishments made clear and trustworthy; raise up a Zhuo Mao from Miyi County, display a Zhu Yi at Tongxiang—then the great enterprise can be attempted and restoration may yet be hoped for."

sentences.zh: 導不能從。

translations.literal: Dao could not follow his advice.
translations.idiomatic: Dao could not act on his advice.

sentences.zh: 劉琨長於招懷而短於撫御，一日之中，雖歸者數千，而去者亦相繼。

translations.literal: Liu Kun excelled at winning people over but fell short in governing them: in a single day, though thousands might come to him, departures followed in unbroken succession.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kun excelled at winning people over but fell short at holding them: in a single day thousands might come to him, yet departures followed one after another.

sentences.zh: 琨遣子遵請兵於代公猗盧，又遣族人高陽內史希合眾於中山，幽州所統代郡、上谷、廣寧之民多歸之，眾至三萬。

translations.literal: Kun sent his son Zun to request troops from Yilu, Duke of Dai, and also sent his clansman He, Interior Administrator of Gaoyang, to gather forces at Zhongshan; the people of Dai, Shanggu, and Guangning—commanderies under You Province—flocked to him in large numbers, until his force reached thirty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Kun sent his son Zun to request troops from Yilu, Duke of Dai, and dispatched his clansman He, Interior Administrator of Gaoyang, to gather forces at Zhongshan; the people of Dai, Shanggu, and Guangning under You Province flocked to him until his force reached thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 王浚怒，遣燕相胡矩督諸軍，與遼西公段疾陸眷共攻希，殺之，驅略三郡士女而去。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was enraged and sent Hu Ju, Chancellor of Yan, to lead the armies, joining with Duan Jilujuan, Duke of Liaoxi, to attack He, kill him, and drive off the men and women of the three commanderies as captives.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun was furious; he sent Hu Ju, Chancellor of Yan, at the head of the armies, joining Duan Jilujuan, Duke of Liaoxi, to attack He, kill him, and carry off the people of the three commanderies.

sentences.zh: 疾陸眷，務勿塵之子也。

translations.literal: Duan Jilujuan was the son of Wuwuchen.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Jilujuan was the son of Wuwuchen.

sentences.zh: 猗盧遣其子六修將兵助琨戍新興。

translations.literal: Yilu sent his son Liujiu at the head of troops to help Kun garrison Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Yilu sent his son Liujiu with troops to help Kun hold Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 琨牙門將邢延以碧石獻琨，琨以與六修，六修復就延求之，不得，執延妻子。

translations.literal: Xing Yan, Liu Kun's Major of the Barracks, presented Kun with a piece of green jade; Kun gave it to Liujiu, who then went back to Yan to ask for it again—when Yan refused, Liujiu seized Yan's wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Yan, Liu Kun's Major of the Barracks, presented Kun with a piece of green jade; Kun gave it to Liujiu, who then went back to Yan to demand it again—when Yan refused, Liujiu seized his wife and children.

sentences.zh: 延怒，以所部兵襲六修，六修走，延遂以新興附漢，請兵以攻并州。

translations.literal: Yan was furious; leading his own troops he attacked Liujiu, who fled; Yan thereupon submitted Xinxing to Han and requested troops to attack Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was enraged; he led his own troops against Liujiu, who fled; Yan then submitted Xinxing to Han and asked for troops to attack Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 李臻之死也，遼東附塞鮮卑素喜連、木丸津托為臻報仇，攻陷諸縣，殺掠士民，屢敗郡兵，連年為寇。

translations.literal: After Li Zhen's death, the frontier Xianbei of Liaodong—Su Xilian and Muwanjin—claimed vengeance for Zhen as their pretext, overran the districts, killed and plundered the people, repeatedly routed the commandery troops, and raided year after year.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Zhen's death, the frontier Xianbei of Liaodong—Su Xilian and Muwanjin—claimed vengeance for Zhen as their pretext, overran the districts, killed and plundered the people, repeatedly routed the commandery troops, and raided year after year.

sentences.zh: 東夷校尉封釋不能討，請與連和，連、津不從。

translations.literal: Feng Shi, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, could not suppress them and requested a peace with Su Xilian; Su Xilian and Muwanjin refused.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shi, Colonel of the Eastern Yi, could not suppress them and sued for peace with Su Xilian; Su Xilian and Muwanjin refused.

sentences.zh: 民失業，歸慕容廆者甚眾，廆稟給遣還，願留者即撫存之。

translations.literal: The people lost their livelihoods; great numbers fled to Murong Hui, who supplied them with provisions and sent them back—those who wished to remain he settled and cared for.
translations.idiomatic: The people lost their livelihoods; great numbers fled to Murong Hui, who supplied them with grain and sent them home—those who wished to stay he settled and cared for.

sentences.zh: 廆少子鷹揚將軍翰言於廆曰：「自古有為之君，莫不尊天子以從民望，成大業。

translations.literal: Murong Han, Hui's youngest son and General Who Displays the Hawk's Pride, said to Hui: "Since antiquity, every ruler who achieved something has honored the Son of Heaven to follow the people's hopes and build a great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Han, Hui's youngest son and General Who Displays the Hawk's Pride, said to Hui: "Since antiquity, every ruler who achieved anything has honored the Son of Heaven to win the people's trust and build a great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 今連、津外以寵本為名，內實幸災為亂。

translations.literal: Now Su Xilian and Muwanjin outwardly take favoring Zhen as their banner, but inwardly they rejoice in disaster and stir rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Now Su Xilian and Muwanjin outwardly take favoring Zhen as their banner, but inwardly they rejoice in disaster and stir rebellion.

sentences.zh: 封使君已誅本請和，而寇暴不已。

translations.literal: Commissioner Feng has already executed the culprit and sought peace, yet their raiding and violence do not cease.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Feng has already put the ringleaders to death and sued for peace, yet their raiding never ceases.

sentences.zh: 中原離亂，州師不振，遼東荒散，莫之救恤，單于不若數其罪而討之。

translations.literal: The Central Plains are torn by chaos, provincial armies cannot respond, Liaodong lies wasted and scattered—with none to rescue or succor it. Great Chanyun, you had best enumerate their crimes and chastise them.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Plains are torn by chaos, provincial armies cannot respond, Liaodong lies wasted and scattered—with none to rescue or succor it. Great Chanyun, you had best enumerate their crimes and chastise them.

sentences.zh: 上則興復遼東，下則併吞二部，忠義彰於本朝，私利歸於我國，此霸王之基也。」

translations.literal: Above, you would restore Liaodong; below, you would absorb both tribes; loyalty and righteousness would shine before the court, and private gain would accrue to our state—this is the foundation of hegemony."
translations.idiomatic: Above, you would restore Liaodong; below, you would absorb both tribes; loyalty and righteousness would shine before the court, and gain would accrue to our state—this is the foundation of hegemony."

sentences.zh: 廆笑曰：「孺子乃能及此乎！」

translations.literal: Hui smiled and said: "Can a lad really reach this level of insight!"
translations.idiomatic: Hui smiled and said: "Can a lad really see this far!"

sentences.zh: 遂帥眾東擊連、津，以翰為前鋒，破斬之，盡並二部之眾。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his forces east to strike Su Xilian and Muwanjin, with Han as vanguard; he defeated and killed them and fully absorbed the forces of both tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he led his forces east against Su Xilian and Muwanjin, with Han as vanguard; he defeated and killed them and fully absorbed both tribes.

sentences.zh: 得所掠民三千餘家，及前歸廆者悉以付郡，遼東賴以復存。

translations.literal: The more than three thousand households they had seized, together with those who had earlier fled to Hui, he all restored to the commandery, and Liaodong was thereby saved from ruin.
translations.idiomatic: The more than three thousand households they had seized, together with those who had earlier fled to Hui, he all restored to the commandery, and Liaodong was thereby saved.

sentences.zh: 封釋疾病，屬其孫弈於廆。

translations.literal: Feng Shi fell ill and entrusted his grandson Yi to Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Shi fell ill and entrusted his grandson Yi to Hui.

sentences.zh: 釋卒，廆召弈與語，說之，曰：「奇士也！」

translations.literal: When Shi died, Hui summoned Yi to speak with him, was delighted with him, and said: "An extraordinary man!"
translations.idiomatic: When Shi died, Hui summoned Yi to talk with him, was delighted, and said: "An extraordinary man!"

sentences.zh: 補小都督。

translations.literal: He appointed him Junior Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He made him Junior Commander.

sentences.zh: 釋子冀州主簿悛、幽州參軍抽來奔喪。

translations.literal: Shi's sons Quan, chief clerk in Ji Province, and Chou, army aide in You Province, came to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: Shi's sons Quan, chief clerk in Ji Province, and Chou, army aide in You Province, came to attend the funeral.

sentences.zh: 廆見之，曰：「此家抎抎千斤犍也。」

translations.literal: Hui saw them and said: "This family produces bullocks a thousand jin in weight, one after another."
translations.idiomatic: Hui saw them and said: "This family turns out thousand-jin bullocks, one after another."

sentences.zh: 以道不通，喪不得還，皆留仕廆，廆以抽為長史，悛為參軍。

translations.literal: Because the roads were blocked, they could not return with the funeral train; all remained to serve Hui, who made Chou Chief Clerk and Quan Army Aide.
translations.idiomatic: Because the roads were blocked, they could not return with the funeral train; all remained to serve Hui, who made Chou Chief Clerk and Quan Army Aide.

sentences.zh: 王浚以妻舅崔毖為東夷校尉。

translations.literal: Wang Jun appointed his wife's brother Cui Bi Colonel of the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun appointed his wife's brother Cui Bi Colonel of the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 毖，琰之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Bi was Cui Yan's great-grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Bi was Cui Yan's great-grandson.
